cfg.h.account.plan: Chooses the quotas read from quotas.json. Public repositories cost no Actions minutes on any plan. Unknown = no quota figures are shown.
cfg.h.act.allow_symlinks: Off = a repository folder that is a symbolic link is refused, so act only reads workflows inside the workspace. On = the link is followed (the workflow file must still sit inside that clone).
cfg.h.act.allowed: Entries repository:file.yml:event, all three exact (for example my-repo:ci.yml:push). Anything not listed is refused.
cfg.h.act.enabled: Off = the act command is only shown. On = a button runs it after you confirm each run; without real secrets.
cfg.h.act.timeout_seconds: The run is stopped when it takes longer.
cfg.h.ai.actions.allowed: From the closed list: rerun_failed, rerun, close_issue, act_local; one per line.
cfg.h.ai.actions.enabled: The answer may contain commands of the closed list; the page shows them and runs nothing.
cfg.h.ai.actions.execute: Adds a confirm button per action; it runs only after you accept the full command. Off by default.
cfg.h.ai.actions.max_per_hour: Most actions that may run in an hour.
cfg.h.ai.actions.ttl_seconds: A proposal can only be confirmed for this long.
cfg.h.ai.allowed_repos: Empty = every repository the monitor watches; or list the allowed ones.
cfg.h.ai.answer_language: Empty = the language of the page.
cfg.h.ai.api_key_env: Name of the environment variable that holds the key; the key itself is never saved.
cfg.h.ai.base_url: https address of an OpenAI-compatible service.
cfg.h.ai.allow_private_targets: OFF by default: an https address that points to a private, local-network or metadata address is refused. Turn it on only for a server of your own network that you trust. An address with a user or an at sign before the host is always refused.
cfg.h.ai.daily_limit: Most calls to the service per day; 0 means none. It also counts the calls of the active notice, which keeps its own limits per hour as well. The notice used to be outside these limits: if it needs more than this total allows, raise the total.
cfg.h.ai.events: build, codeql, report: one per line.
cfg.h.ai.max_input_chars: Most characters of data sent to the model.
cfg.h.ai.max_output_chars: The answer is cut at this length.
cfg.h.ai.model: Name of the model to ask.
cfg.h.ai.ollama_url: Address of the Ollama service on this computer.
cfg.h.ai.provider: none is off; an outside service receives data from your repositories.
cfg.h.ai.skill: The core of the guide of the AI of the monitor (skills/internal/SKILL.md: what the monitor is, what it may read, what it must never do, how to diagnose a red run) is added to every prompt. Turn it off for a very small local model.
cfg.h.ai.skill_max_chars: The most characters of the guide that are added to a prompt. A small local model with a context of 4k to 8k tokens: 1500; a provider API: 4000.
cfg.h.ai.timeout_seconds: Seconds to wait for the model before giving up.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.brief_max_bytes: ALERTS_BRIEF.md never exceeds this many bytes (2048 by default).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.cascade.enabled: On = an alert that is red because another repository is red (its log names it, or a rule in ai_alerts.cascade.map) is listed under that one in the brief.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.block_on_sto: Off. On = at the end of a turn with real alerts open the AI is asked once to look at them (not more than once per cooldown).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.cooldown_min: Shortest time between two requests at the end of a turn.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.enabled: On = the script installed with bin/monitor_cli.py ai-hook install adds the brief to the AI session when real alerts are open.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.max_chars: Upper limit of the text the gate script adds.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.max_lines: Lines of the brief the gate script puts in the AI session.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.stale_hours: The gate script warns the AI when the brief is older than this many hours (the monitor may be stopped).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.diagnose.enabled: Off. On = for a new red run the monitor reads its job list and the end of its log from GitHub (read only calls, counted in your allowance) and puts the failing step and about ten relevant lines in the feed.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.diagnose.log_lines: How many relevant lines of the log go into each alert (10 by default).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.diagnose.max_bytes: A diagnosis never exceeds this many bytes once cleaned of secrets.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.diagnose.max_per_cycle: Upper limit of runs read per cycle; the rest wait for the next one.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.enabled: Local files only (ai_alerts.jsonl and ALERTS_BRIEF.md); no network. An AI reads the brief when it starts.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.folder: Empty = the ai/ folder of the monitor. Choose a folder your AI sessions read.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.heartbeat.enabled: On = a small local file records the last read (stream, MCP server, gate script, endpoint) and the bottom bar shows it.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.heartbeat.window_minutes: Minutes after the last read during which the bottom bar says an AI is connected.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.briefs.access_log: Off. On = keeps a short record of which brief of a tab an AI read and when (no secret, no text of the brief).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.hook.enabled: Off. On = a POST with a closed list of cleaned fields to the local address below.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.hook.max_per_hour: Upper limit; more alerts wait in the feed.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.stream.enabled: Off. On = GET /api/ai/stream sends the alerts as events (read only; in the network mode with the access token).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.stream.max_clients: More listeners than this get a 'too many' answer.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.stream.max_seconds: A stream ends after this time; the AI tool reconnects.
cfg.h.compare.cache_seconds: How long an answer is reused before it is computed again; 0 computes it every time.
cfg.h.compare.default_days_filter: all, workdays or weekend: which days of the week the figures count (see Workdays).
cfg.h.compare.default_window_days: Length of the period compared when none is asked: 7 for a week, 30 for a month. The score ledger keeps two of them.
cfg.h.compare.enabled: Turns on the comparison of this period with the one before, from what the monitor already holds. Off by default; nothing is read from GitHub.
cfg.t.compare.enabled: You will see: the Compare periods tab, with the change of failed runs, duration, resolution time and score. Cost: no extra GitHub calls.
cfg.t.updates.check: You will see: the Updates menu can list the published versions with their notes. Cost: one read-only request a day. Needs gh signed in; it is skipped while the monitor is offline.
cfg.t.screens.enabled: You will see: the wall-screen pages answer instead of 404, so a TV or a second monitor can show them without a menu. Cost: none; they only read what the monitor holds.
cfg.t.sentinels.security.enabled: You will see: the Security sentinel tab with the alerts of Dependabot, code scanning and secret scanning, the protection of the default branch and the permissions of the workflows. Cost: a few read-only requests per repository each round, inside the call budget of the sentinel; nothing is written.
cfg.t.sentinels.supply.enabled: You will see: the Supply chain sentinel tab with the actions that are not pinned to a commit, the references that can move, the wide permissions and the risky triggers. Cost: it reads the workflow files of each repository (a few read-only requests, inside the call budget); nothing is cloned or written.
cfg.t.sentinels.delivery.enabled: You will see: the Delivery sentinel tab with what was built but not delivered: tags without a release, releases without notes, versions that disagree and assets that are missing. Cost: it reads the latest releases, tags and the files you name of each repository (a few read-only requests, inside the call budget); nothing is written.
cfg.t.sentinels.collab.enabled: You will see: the Collab sentinel tab with the open issues and pull requests, the ones that wait too long and the conflicts. Cost: the lists of issues and pull requests of each repository, read page by page (up to pagination.collab_pages), and a few detail requests per round; nothing is written.
cfg.t.runners.model.enabled: You will see: in Settings > Advanced the queue and the cost by kind of runner, the workflows that fire themselves again and again and the jobs waiting for a self-hosted runner that is not there. Cost: up to runners.model.jobs_per_cycle unfinished runs per cycle are read, one request each; read only.
cfg.t.ai.assistant.enabled: You will see: in the Alerts tab a panel of fixed questions that the AI answers from the data of the monitor, with its sources. Cost: one call to your AI provider for each question you press (none in the background); it only reads and never acts.
cfg.t.ai.similar.enabled: You will see: "explain this alert" also lists the alerts that look like it, open ones and resolved ones. Cost: none; a plain comparison of words on this computer, no model and no request.
cfg.t.ai.prompt_log.enabled: You will see: nothing on the page; an administrator can read or empty the file ai_prompts.jsonl. Cost: a small file on this computer, limited to ai.prompt_log.keep entries; secrets and hidden words are removed before writing, and the file is not in the backup or in the zip.
cfg.t.live.sse.enabled: You will see: nothing in the page itself; a client can open GET /api/live-events/stream and receive the webhook events as they arrive. Cost: one open connection for each listener; it only reads, and in the network mode it needs the access token.
cfg.h.compare.include_in_report: Adds a short comparison to the scheduled reports. Off by default.
cfg.h.compare.min_days_of_history: The monitor must have watched this long before the period to compare against is used.
cfg.h.compare.min_repo_runs: A repository needs this many finished runs in both periods to appear in the list of changes.
cfg.h.compare.min_resolved: With fewer alerts resolved in a period there is no resolution time.
cfg.h.compare.min_runs_per_window: With fewer finished runs in a period, its figures say there is not enough data.
cfg.h.compare.min_snapshots: With fewer hourly snapshots of the score in a period there is no mean score.
cfg.h.compare.top_changes: How many rows each list of changes shows (repositories and workflows).
cfg.h.compare.workdays: Days of the week that count as workdays, Monday = 1 to Sunday = 7. Bank holidays are not known.
cfg.h.discovery.fork_checks_per_pass: Each check costs one or two requests; the answer is kept for a week. On an account with hundreds of forks the list fills in over a few listings.
cfg.h.discovery.min_keep_pct: A listing of the account that comes back empty, or with fewer than this percentage of the repositories of the last good one, is not believed: the last good listing is kept, the listing is read again and the brief says so. 0 = every listing is believed.
cfg.h.fleet.page_size: How many repositories the fleet view draws at a time (10 to 500). The page keeps all the rows and draws only one page, so a fleet of hundreds of repositories does not slow it down.
cfg.h.fleet.group_by: ecosystem (default): by the ecosystem of the repository. label: by the labels of 'Labels by repository name' (this is how organisations or teams are told apart). state: bad, warning, OK, not seen. none: one list.
cfg.h.fleet.sort: risk (default): the repositories that need a person first. name: alphabetical. last_run: the most recent run first. state: the worst state first.
cfg.h.fleet.labels: One entry per line as pattern=label, for example team-*=backend or *-docs=docs. The first pattern that fits the name of a repository gives its label; * and ? stand for any text. Empty by default.
cfg.h.fleet.saved_filters: One entry per line as name=severity|ecosystem|label|text (every part after the name may be empty), for example attention=bad||backend|. They appear in the fleet view as ready-made filters.
cfg.h.discovery.fork_ci_days: Days. 0 = an enabled workflow is enough. Used when forks are only watched if they have a CI of their own.
cfg.h.discovery.fork_policy: show: watch every fork (default). skip: watch none. skip_unless_ci: watch only the forks that have a CI of their own (an enabled workflow and a recent run). auto: like skip_unless_ci, with a window twice as long on an organisation. Forks waiting to be checked are left out until they are.
cfg.h.discovery.skip_archived: On (default): an archived repository cannot run workflows, so it is not watched. Off: archived repositories are watched like any other.
cfg.h.lint.own_owners: One per line. The account being watched always counts; add the others here (for example an organisation you belong to). A finding of unpinned_uses says whether the action is own or third-party.
cfg.h.lint.unpinned_own: same: like any other action (default). info: only as information. ignore: not listed. Third-party actions are always listed.
cfg.h.live.sse.enabled: Off. On = GET /api/live-events/stream sends the webhook events as they arrive (read only; in the network mode with the access token).
cfg.h.live.sse.max_clients: More listeners than this get a 'too many' answer.
cfg.h.live.sse.max_seconds: A live stream ends after this time; the client reconnects.
cfg.h.ai_notify.confirmed_provider: Nothing is sent until you type here the name of the provider chosen in the AI block (for example anthropic); if you change the provider, confirm again. Type command to confirm the outgoing command.
cfg.h.ai_notify.cost_per_call_cents: The cost per call that you declare, in cents (the monitor cannot know the price of your plan); it is added up against the cost cap.
cfg.h.ai_notify.enabled: Off by default. When a NEW real alert opens, a short summary (a closed list of fields, redacted) goes to the provider of the AI block and its answer is kept as advice in ai_notify.jsonl; the AI never runs anything. It needs the confirmation below and the key in the variable named in the AI block, and it respects both caps.
cfg.h.ai_notify.max_calls_per_hour: Cap of calls to the provider in one hour; a call is counted before it is made.
cfg.h.ai_notify.max_cost_per_hour_cents: No notice goes out if it would take the declared cost of the last hour over this figure.
cfg.h.airgapped: On = no request leaves for the update check (it is turned off). The GitHub data you asked for are still read through gh.
cfg.h.alerts.mute_hours: How long an alert, a rule or a sentinel stays silenced when you silence it from the Alerts tab (1 to 720).
cfg.h.analytics.enabled: Durations, queue time, steps and flaky workflows.
cfg.h.analytics.flaky: Labels a workflow that failed and then passed on the same commit; it never changes what counts as red.
cfg.h.analytics.jobs_per_cycle: Completed runs whose jobs are read each cycle; 0 reads none.
cfg.h.analytics.keep_days: Days of daily figures kept for the trend.
cfg.h.analytics.max_samples: Samples kept per workflow (the oldest are dropped).
cfg.h.analytics.min_samples: A workflow shows figures only with this many samples.
cfg.h.analytics.slow_factor: A workflow is flagged when its p50 is this many times its usual one.
cfg.h.analytics.steps: Also keep the duration of each step of the jobs.
cfg.h.audit_dir: Folder where the daily reports and the audit files are.
cfg.h.audit_log.enabled: Writes who changed what (settings, silences, users, credentials) to a file with a chain of hashes, so a line that is changed or cut out is noticed. It keeps names, never values or secrets.
cfg.h.audit_log.keep_generations: Default 5 (1 to 20). When the file passes its size it becomes .1, the old .1 becomes .2 and so on; what is older than this many files is deleted, and the chain is checked across all of them.
cfg.h.audit_log.required: Off by default. On: an action that has to be recorded (the confirmations of the actions on GitHub, the login, the mode, the silences...) is refused with a 503 while the log of actions cannot be written. The settings stay open so that it can be put right.
cfg.h.audit_log.maintainers_can_read: Off: only an administrator reads the log of actions. On: a maintainer reads it too.
cfg.h.audit_log.max_mb: Past this size the old part is kept as one more file and the chain goes on in a new one.
cfg.h.auth.allow_bearer: Lets a script or an app sign in with POST /api/auth/login {"client": "api"} and send the token as Authorization: Bearer. Off by default: only the browser signs in. Turn it on only for scripts and apps you trust.
cfg.h.auth.audit: Writes who signed in, who failed, who was locked and every refused request to auth_audit.jsonl (never a password or a token). Admins read it at /api/auth/audit.
cfg.h.auth.enabled: Off by default: one person uses the monitor with no login. On: once the first administrator exists (created from this computer, at /login), every request needs a session. Roles: viewer reads, maintainer also silences and acknowledges, admin also changes settings and users. The lite edition never has a login.
cfg.h.auth.lockout_minutes: Minutes a user stays locked after too many wrong passwords (1-1440).
cfg.h.auth.max_failed_logins: Wrong passwords for one user before that user is locked (3-20). A lock ends by itself after the lock time.
cfg.h.auth.min_length: Characters a new password needs at least (8-64). Passwords are kept only as a salted scrypt hash.
cfg.h.auth.session_hours: Hours a login stays valid (1-720). After that the person signs in again.
cfg.h.cache.etag.enabled: A read that did not change answers 304 and costs no quota.
cfg.h.cache.etag.ttl_hours: After this long an endpoint is read again in full.
cfg.h.cache.etag.skip_stateful: On by default. Jobs of a run, a single run, check suites and check runs describe something that is still changing, so they are never read with If-None-Match: a 304 on them could show an old state. Costs a little quota.
cfg.h.cache.etag.revalidate_active: On by default. When the last list of runs of a repository still had a run queued or in progress, the next read is made in full instead of asking if it changed, so a finished run is never missed because of an old 304.
cfg.h.cache.negative_ttl_s: Seconds. A repository that answered 404 or 403 (not a rate limit) is not asked again for this long. 0 = never remembered. A repository that gets the permission back is read again after this time.
cfg.h.central.max_age_minutes: A central panel file older than this (120 by default) is shown as "behind" and not trusted: its reds are ignored.
cfg.h.central.source: Off by default. Reads data/sentinel.json of your profile repository, which a workflow refreshes every half hour with its own token, so it spends none of your allowance: git = fetch of your local clone (no API call at all), http = the raw file. It is the base line of reds, release candidates and signatures, shown as "source: central panel, N min ago"; in Low mode only the repositories it says are red, those with a run in progress and the security panels it does not carry are asked live.
cfg.h.channel_on: Switches this channel on or off.
cfg.h.check_on: Switches this check on or off.
cfg.h.cold_refresh_seconds: Time between two reads of the cold repositories.
cfg.h.cold_runs_per_repo: Runs read for each cold repository.
cfg.h.discover_limit: Most repositories listed for the account (raise it for hundreds or thousands).
cfg.h.discover_refresh_seconds: Time between two searches for new repositories.
cfg.h.discovery.auto_frequency: Quiet accounts are read less often and busy ones more often, always inside the call budget. Your own intervals are the base. Off by default.
cfg.h.discovery.events: Compares the list of the account at each listing; the first look after a start is not news.
cfg.h.discovery.hide: One per line: fork, empty, private. Archived repositories are always left out.
cfg.h.discovery.suggest_groups: When three or more share a prefix. A group is only added after you confirm, and the file is copied first.
cfg.h.dispatch.required_ci: Workflow file names (for example ci.yml). A commit counts as green only when each of them succeeded on it; the default is ci.yml. Lists per repository: dispatch.required_ci_repos in the file.
cfg.h.display.blink_red_tiles: The tiles at the top (and the items of the bar at the foot) that turn red blink softly until the cause is solved. With reduced motion in the system they show a fixed thicker red edge instead.
cfg.h.display.timezone: Zone of the times written for people (log, reports, command line, notifications): local = this computer, utc, or a name such as Europe/Madrid. Machine fields stay in UTC.
cfg.h.ecosystems: Only the repositories of these ecosystems are watched (with repositories = all).
cfg.h.ecosystems_file: JSON file that names your ecosystems and their repository prefixes.
cfg.h.exclude: Repositories never watched, one name per line.
cfg.h.extra_reader.any_folder: Off by default: the file of the second account must live under the accounts folder of the monitor (accounts/, or the folder named by MONITOR_ACCOUNTS_DIR) and is never reached through a link. Turn it on only if the file must stay somewhere else; the path is then still a plain file, never a network path and never on the D: drive.
cfg.h.extra_reader.enabled: Off by default. The reads are spread over your login, the GitHub App (if on) and a second account with a read-only token, by the calls each one has left. Writes and actions never use it.
cfg.h.extra_reader.file: ONLY the path of a text file whose first line is a fine-grained token with read-only permissions, kept outside any repository and readable only by you. The monitor reads it at the moment of use, keeps it only in memory and never stores, prints or logs it.
cfg.h.finops.jobs_per_cycle: 0 = the system of every job is assumed (Settings > Basic). More = the labels of each job are read for the right multiplier (Linux, Windows, macOS, larger runners), one call per run.
cfg.h.github_actions.allowed: Names: rerun_failed, rerun_run, rerun_job, cancel, close_issue, close_pr, merge_pr. By default only rerun_failed and cancel.
cfg.h.github_actions.enabled: Off = the monitor only reads. On = buttons to run again, cancel, close or merge; each action shows exactly what will be sent and asks you to confirm it.
cfg.h.github_actions.merge_method: Used by merge_pr: squash, merge or rebase.
cfg.h.github_app.app_id: The number of the App, shown on its page in GitHub (Settings, Developer settings, GitHub Apps). Digits only.
cfg.h.github_app.enabled: Off by default. The reads of the monitor use the token of an App installed on your account, which has its own allowance (separate from yours, and bigger the more repositories it covers). Writes and actions keep using your token. If the App fails or lacks a permission, the read is made again with your token.
cfg.h.github_app.installation_id: Leave empty: the monitor finds the installation by itself. Fill it in only when the App is installed on several accounts.
cfg.h.github_app.key_path: ONLY the path of the .pem file of the App, kept outside any repository and readable only by you. The monitor never reads, copies, prints or logs the key: it hands the path to the program openssl, which signs the short-lived JWT.
cfg.h.github_app.openssl_path: Optional. Absolute path of openssl when the monitor does not find it by itself (it looks in the PATH, then where Git for Windows keeps it). Leave it empty to search.
cfg.h.github_app.share_reads: Lets `python bin/monitor_cli.py gh-token --read-only` print a one-hour installation token of the GitHub App on this computer, so that the `gh` of your tools and agents reads with the allowance of the App and not with yours. The token goes to the standard output only, never to a file or a log. Give the App read-only permissions. Off by default.
cfg.h.github_owner: Account whose repositories are watched; empty uses the account of gh.
cfg.h.github_token.enabled: Off = the monitor uses your own gh login. On = a token you paste in Advanced is kept in the secure store of the system (never in a file of settings or a log).
cfg.h.github_token.store: auto = the system store (Windows DPAPI, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service) and a file with permissions 600 only when it is missing; system or file force one.
cfg.h.hot_hours: A repository stays hot this long after its last push or run.
cfg.h.issues_refresh_seconds: Time between two reads of the open build issues.
cfg.h.language: Language of the page, the reports and the tools; empty follows the system.
cfg.h.lessons.allow_write: Off: the library (config/lessons.json) can only be edited by hand. On: an administrator can add a lesson with POST /api/ai/lessons (after confirming it), and the MCP server started with --allow-lessons can do the same. Nothing is ever written to GitHub.
cfg.h.lessons.brief_max_bytes: The most bytes of the compact text an AI reads (and of the brief before a push).
cfg.h.lessons.enabled: Writes one line to a local file (data/failures.jsonl) for every failure that the feed of alerts opens, files it under a category and builds ai/LESSONS.md and GET /api/ai/lessons from it. Nothing is sent anywhere. It needs ai_alerts.enabled.
cfg.h.lessons.max_entries: When the file has more lines than this, the oldest are dropped.
cfg.h.lessons.recurring_from: Failures of one kind in 7 days from which it is called repeated and a guard is proposed.
cfg.h.lessons.retention_days: Lines of the book older than this are dropped. The trend compares 7 days with the 7 before, so keep at least 14.
cfg.h.lint.enabled: Reads the workflow files of your local clones and, when the source is auto or sparse, of the other repositories from GitHub; nothing is written anywhere.
cfg.h.lint.ignore: repository:file:rule, with * for any, one per line (for example demo-*:ci.yml:secrets_in_clear).
cfg.h.lint.in_report: Adds one line to the daily report when there are findings.
cfg.h.lint.refresh_seconds: Time between two scans of the clones.
cfg.h.listen.allowed_hosts: Host names or addresses accepted in the Host header, besides this computer's own (protects against DNS rebinding).
cfg.h.listen.host: A private address of this computer or 0.0.0.0 (every interface). A public address is refused.
cfg.h.listen.local_port: 0 = off. With a reverse proxy declared (public name, Secure cookie or trusted proxy) nothing that arrives on the main port counts as this computer, so the settings that decide exposure cannot be changed from there. A number from 1024 to 65535 opens a second port that only listens on 127.0.0.1: use it from this computer to change those settings. It still asks for the access token. Needs a restart.
cfg.h.listen.max_failed_attempts: After this many wrong tokens within a minute, that address is refused for five minutes.
cfg.h.listen.network: Off = only 127.0.0.1. On = also the address below, with an access token for every request and a warning in the page. Needs a restart. Warning: without HTTPS the token and the data travel unencrypted; set a certificate (listen.tls_cert_file) or an HTTPS proxy before you use it. First steps: turn listen.query_access off, and use HTTPS or a VPN.
cfg.h.listen.proxy_public_host: For an HTTPS proxy on the default port (443) that forwards Host and Origin without a port: the one host name to accept as it is. Empty = none. It only counts when HTTPS is on (direct, or with the access cookie marked Secure). Never an address with a port, a path or a user.
cfg.h.listen.query_access: Deprecated and off by default. When on, the ?access= address opens the session once, but the token stays in the history, the logs and the Referer. Turn it off to open the session only with POST /api/access (the token in the body) or the header.
cfg.h.listen.secure_cookie: Turn on when an HTTPS proxy sits in front of the monitor (direct HTTPS marks it on its own). The token does not replace encryption: on a network you do not control, use HTTPS.
cfg.h.listen.tls_cert_file: Optional. With the key below, the monitor serves HTTPS itself using YOUR certificate (TLS 1.2 or newer). If the files cannot be used the monitor does not start. Needs a restart.
cfg.h.listen.tls_key_file: The key that goes with the certificate. Keep it outside the monitor folder; it is never shown or copied.
cfg.h.listen.token_env: The NAME of the variable (16 characters or more in its value). Without it a random token is made at each start and shown once in the console.
cfg.h.listen.trusted_proxy: Off by default. Only turn it on if a reverse proxy of YOURS on this same computer is the only way into the monitor. Then a failed attempt is counted against the last address of X-Forwarded-For (the one your proxy adds) instead of against the proxy, so one person's wrong tokens do not lock out everybody. The proxy MUST add the real client address (nginx: proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;) and MUST run on this same computer: the monitor believes that header on any connection that arrives over loopback. Wrong tokens on requests that arrive without a usable X-Forwarded-For are also counted together, with a limit three times higher; that shared lock never stops a request that carries the right token. SECURITY: a request that comes through a proxy is never treated as this computer. If anybody else can reach the monitor directly, leave it off: a client could write that header.
cfg.h.listen.trusted_proxies: Empty by default. Only with 'Trust the reverse proxy in front' on. Addresses or networks (for example 172.29.77.0/24) of a proxy that is in another container or on another machine: a connection from them, or from this computer, has its X-Forwarded-For believed to count the failed attempts, so one person's wrong tokens do not lock out everybody. It never makes a request count as this computer.
cfg.h.logs.failed_step.enabled: Adds a button to the alerts of a failed run that reads, only when you press it, the jobs and the failed log of that run from GitHub (two calls of your allowance) and shows the failing step and its last relevant lines, cleaned of tokens, keys, addresses and the home folder. Off by default. Administrators only in the team mode.
cfg.h.logs.failed_step.lines: How many relevant lines of the failed log are shown.
cfg.h.logs.failed_step.max_bytes: The most bytes of text shown for one failed step.
cfg.h.logs.failed_step.max_per_minute: The most runs per minute whose failed step is read from GitHub (a press of the button on a run already read costs nothing). Protects your allowance when somebody asks for many different runs.
cfg.h.max_workers: Requests to GitHub made at the same time.
cfg.h.min_rate_remaining: Below this allowance the monitor slows down to leave quota to you.
cfg.h.mirror.enabled: Off = nothing is downloaded. On = the artifacts of finished runs are copied into the folder below, within the size ceiling.
cfg.h.mirror.folder: A folder on this computer (never a network path, never the D: drive).
cfg.h.mirror.keep_days: Copies older than this are deleted.
cfg.h.mirror.max_mb: Total size of the folder; the oldest copies are deleted first.
cfg.h.mirror.max_per_cycle: Limits the downloads (and the API calls) of each cycle.
cfg.h.mode: Full reads every run list; lite reads fewer runs to save API calls.
cfg.h.modes.auto_low: Goes to Low mode when the calls left fall under the entry number and comes back over the exit number or at the renewal.
cfg.h.modes.auto_low_enter: Default 1000. Must be lower than the exit number (otherwise the defaults are used, so it cannot flap).
cfg.h.modes.low.hot_hours: Default 2: fewer repositories are read at the short interval.
cfg.h.modes.low.refresh_seconds: Default 240 (4 minutes). A slower value of yours in the normal settings is never made faster.
cfg.h.modes.low.runs_per_repo: Default 10: short lists cost the same call but less to process.
cfg.h.network.etag: On by default. A read that answers 304 costs no allowance. Together with cache.etag.enabled: if either is off, every read is a plain read. Needs a restart.
cfg.h.network.graphql_batch: From 1 to 30 (20 by default): how many repositories one GraphQL query asks for.
cfg.h.network.graphql_checks: Off by default. Repositories that are not hot are read in batches with GraphQL, which has an allowance of its own, instead of one REST call each; hot repositories and any repository that GraphQL does not answer are still read through REST. Trade-off: only the last commit of the default branch is seen (a workflow that did not run on it is not listed) and there are no durations, attempts or other branches. See QUOTA.md.
cfg.h.network.use_proxy: Off = outgoing notifications ignore http_proxy and https_proxy. On = they use them, and the destination (and every redirect) is checked before the proxy gets the request. The proxy resolves the name again on its own, so it is a frontier of trust: turn this on only behind a managed proxy that refuses loopback, private, link-local and metadata destinations.
cfg.h.notify.allow_private_targets: Off = a destination that is, or resolves to, this computer or the local network (127.x, 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x with the cloud metadata address, ::1, fc00::/7) is refused, also after a redirect. On = a Matrix server in your own network is allowed.
cfg.h.notify.digest.max_items: A user's digest keeps at most this many alerts they have not seen; the oldest are dropped first.
cfg.h.notify.enabled: Nothing leaves this computer until this is on and a channel is on.
cfg.h.notify.events: red_new, stuck_new, pending_sign, offline, online, workflow_failed...; one per line.
cfg.h.notify.max_per_hour: At most this many messages leave the computer in an hour.
cfg.h.notify.users.enabled: Team mode only. Each user chooses channel, sentinels, lowest level and digest; the role decides what they may be told. Off by default, and nothing is sent until a user turns it on and sets a destination.
cfg.h.notify.users.max_per_hour: At most this many messages are sent to one user in an hour; the digest counts as one.
cfg.h.open_browser: Off = the page is only served; open the address printed on the console.
cfg.h.config_check.strict: Off = at the start the monitor names every key that nobody reads (a typo, with the closest key), every value of the wrong type and every number out of range, and starts anyway. On = it names them and does not start.
cfg.h.organizations.discover: Off = only your account is looked at. On = the organisations you belong to are listed in Basic so you can choose what to watch (one read a day).
cfg.h.otlp.enabled: Off = nothing is sent. On = traces and metrics of the runs go to the collector below.
cfg.h.otlp.endpoint: HTTPS anywhere, or plain HTTP only on this computer (for example http://127.0.0.1:4318). The OTLP/HTTP JSON protocol.
cfg.h.otlp.interval_seconds: Each export sends only the runs not sent before.
cfg.h.outputs.dashboard.enabled: Serves the ci_red document for a status dashboard on 127.0.0.1.
cfg.h.outputs.json.enabled: Serves the tables for Grafana's JSON data source on 127.0.0.1.
cfg.h.outputs.prometheus.enabled: Serves /metrics on 127.0.0.1 only; no token, no API quota.
cfg.h.outputs.prometheus.per_repo: Adds one series per repository and workflow; more series, more detail.
cfg.h.p.apprise_env: NAME of the environment variable that holds the Apprise addresses (separated by spaces or commas); they are never saved. Apprise opens its own connections: the guard of the monitor on private addresses does not apply to it.
cfg.h.p.chat_id: Numeric id of the chat that receives the messages.
cfg.h.p.days: Age or window in days for this check.
cfg.h.p.homeserver: https address of your Matrix server.
cfg.h.p.local_url: http address on this computer that receives a POST of the event.
cfg.h.p.max_mb: Total size of live artifacts above which it is reported.
cfg.h.p.max_per_tick: Most items examined in one cycle.
cfg.h.p.minutes: Minutes a run waits before it counts as stuck.
cfg.h.p.recent_days: Only releases newer than this are checked.
cfg.h.p.retention_days: Retention in days above which an artifact is reported.
cfg.h.p.room: Internal id of the room, starting with !.
cfg.h.p.sender: Address the mail comes from (name@host). The relay on this computer needs no login.
cfg.h.p.server: https address of the ntfy server (or one on this computer, http://127.0.0.1:port). The topic and the token of each user are set by the user.
cfg.h.p.severity: info, warn or bad: how the finding is shown and counted.
cfg.h.p.token_env: NAME of the environment variable that holds the token; the token is never saved.
cfg.h.p.topic: MQTT topic that receives the events (for lights and beacons).
cfg.h.p.url_env: NAME of the environment variable that holds the webhook URL; the URL is never saved.
cfg.h.ports.complete: The port the complete edition listens on (8765 by default): a whole number from 1024 to 65535. It applies at the next start. The start, the check that another monitor is not already on it, the doctor, the health check, the command line, the terminal views, the launchers and the service all read this number; --port on the command line and MONITOR_PORT win over it.
cfg.h.ports.lite: The port the lite edition listens on (8766 by default): a whole number from 1024 to 65535. It applies at the next start. It must not be the port of the complete edition; --port on the command line wins over it.
cfg.h.profiles_file: JSON file with the batch profiles.
cfg.h.quota.alert_percent: The second, stronger warning of the month.
cfg.h.quota.billing_api: Read only, off by default. It needs a login with permission to see billing; on a 403 or 404 the monitor keeps the estimate and says so.
cfg.h.quota.default_runner: Linux counts 1x, Windows and macOS count more (the rates are in quotas.json). Only an estimate: the runner of each job is not always known.
cfg.h.quota.warn_percent: Said once per month, through the notifications. Only for private repositories.
cfg.h.refresh_seconds: Time between two reads of the hot repositories.
cfg.h.report_history_days: How many daily reports are kept for the yesterday-versus-today view.
cfg.h.report_schedule.cron: Five fields: minute, hour, day of the month, month and day of the week, in the local time of this computer. 0 8 * * 1 is every Monday at 8:00.
cfg.h.report_schedule.enabled: Writes a report (HTML and Markdown) on the schedule below. Off by default; nothing is sent anywhere, the files stay in the data folder.
cfg.h.report_schedule.formats: html, markdown or both. A PDF is the print-to-PDF of the browser on the HTML page.
cfg.h.report_schedule.keep: How many runs of reports are kept; older ones are removed when a new one is written.
cfg.h.report_schedule.top: How many repositories and alerts the report lists (the worst first).
cfg.h.reports.max_calls_per_cycle: The calls to GitHub that the optional reports may spend in one cycle, all of them together. A low number reads few repositories each time.
cfg.h.reports.queue.enabled: Reads the jobs of a few finished runs that waited (one read for each, inside reports.max_calls_per_cycle) and says how long a job waited before it started for each kind of runner: Linux, Windows, macOS, larger and self-hosted. Off by default.
cfg.h.reports.release_view.enabled: From what the Sentinel already knows (no call): a repository is ready when it has entries in its changelog or a green build that nobody released, and nothing is red and no signature is waiting; it is blocked, with the reason, when a workflow is red or a signature waits. Needs the Sentinel. Off by default.
cfg.h.reports.supply_chain.enabled: Reads the latest release of a few repositories each cycle (one read each, inside reports.max_calls_per_cycle) and says by the names of its files whether it carries a software bill of materials (SBOM), checksums and a signature or attestation. The files are never downloaded. Off by default.
cfg.h.reports.workflow_hygiene.enabled: Reads the workflow files of a few repositories each cycle from GitHub (one read for the folder and one for each file, inside reports.max_calls_per_cycle) and lists what is badly written: actions not pinned to a commit, permissions not limited, a job without timeout-minutes, no concurrency group, pull_request_target and injection risks, secrets in clear. Each repository is read again after a day. Off by default.
cfg.h.ci.rerun_timing: Off by default. The time of a re-run is always measured from its own attempt (never from the first try, which could be days or months old); with this on, the monitor also asks GitHub for the real duration of each finished re-run (a few extra calls per repository and cycle, remembered afterwards).
cfg.h.ci.red_events: Only a failed run of one of these events counts as red on a branch (default: push, schedule, workflow_dispatch, merge_group, workflow_run, repository_dispatch). Pull requests, comments and issues never do, so a failing pull request cannot turn the main branch red. A chained workflow (workflow_run, repository_dispatch) counts only on the default branch and when it does not come from a fork.
cfg.h.ci.count_fork_runs: Off by default: a run of a pull request that comes from a fork never makes the branch red, even when the branch of the fork is also called main. Turn it on only if you want those runs counted.
cfg.h.ci.automation_counts: Off by default: workflows that only react to issues, comments or labels (triage, bots) are told apart by the events they run on and do not count as red CI.
cfg.h.ci.inactive_days: A workflow that failed but has not run for this many days is shown as inactive, not as red for ever. 0 turns it off.
cfg.h.ci.dormant_repos: On by default. A repository that has never run anything of its own is dormant, and one whose newest run is older than the days of the inactivity limit above is inactive: neither is green and neither is red. They are counted apart (header figures, the data of the score) and the score is calculated only from what runs. Off: they are not counted.
cfg.h.ci.red_ages: On by default. A workflow that failed on the branch and has not run again for the days below stops being red and is shown as inactive: a failure nobody attends to for weeks is history, not an alarm that never ends (a cron copied from another repository that fails every night and was then switched off is the typical case). Off: a red stays red until the workflow runs green again.
cfg.h.ci.red_age_days: Default 30. A failed run older than this many days, with nothing newer of the events that decide, no longer makes its branch red. Used only while the switch above is on.
cfg.h.ci.forks_need_own_ci: On by default. A fork copies the files, the settings and the workflows of a project somebody else owns, so its hygiene (ruleset, releases, changelog, licence), its workflow files and the nightly jobs it inherits say nothing about your work. With this on, a fork enters the hygiene panel, the lint of workflows and the score only when it has a CI of its own (see the days below); the others are counted apart and not judged. Off: every fork is judged like any other repository.
cfg.h.ci.fork_own_ci_days: Default 90. A fork has a CI of its own when it ran a push, pull request, manual or merge queue run of its own in this many days. A copied schedule does not count. If the list of its runs is full and does not reach back that far, the fork stays in. Used only while the switch above is on.
cfg.h.ci.extra_branches: Patterns of extra branches whose last run also counts (for example release-*). Empty by default: only the default branch is watched. The merge queue of the default branch is always watched and labelled.
cfg.h.repos: all discovers the repositories of the account; or list the names to watch.
cfg.h.retention.analytics_days: Days of the analytics history older than this are removed. Default 180.
cfg.h.retention.enabled: Removes (or archives) the events and the analytics history older than the limits below, so a monitor that runs for months does not grow without a ceiling. It never touches the configuration, the state of the sentinels or the silences. On by default.
cfg.h.retention.events_days: Events older than this many days are removed (or archived, see the mode). Default 90.
cfg.h.retention.events_max_kb: With the file backend the feed file is cut to its newest half when it grows beyond this size, whatever its age. Default 512. Needs a restart.
cfg.h.retention.interval_hours: How often the purge runs: a short pass at the end of a refresh once this time has passed. Default 24.
cfg.h.retention.mode: delete = remove them. archive = first write them to a compressed file in events/archive/ (outside the hot path), then remove them from the feed. Default archive.
cfg.h.retention.warn_events_mb: --doctor warns when the events of an account take more than this. Default 20.
cfg.h.rp_prefer: Which source answers this kind of read first: auto (the one with the most calls left), user, app or extra. If it fails or is under its reserve the others answer. Writes and actions always use the user.
cfg.h.rp_reserve: The monitor does not read with this source while it has no more calls left than this, if another source can. Use it to leave calls to the user for the gh of your tools and agents. 0 = no reserve.
cfg.h.rule_on: Switches this rule on or off.
cfg.h.runners.enabled: Off = not read. On = idle, busy or offline for each runner of the account (one extra read per cycle).
cfg.h.runners.scope: owner = the runners of the account or organisation; repos = those of each watched repository (more calls).
cfg.h.runners.model.enabled: Off = nothing is read. On = the labels (runs-on) of the jobs tell hosted, larger, paid third-party and self-hosted runners apart; the Advanced tab shows the queue and the cost by kind, the workflows that fire themselves again and again and the jobs that wait for a self-hosted runner that is not there. Read only.
cfg.h.runners.model.jobs_per_cycle: Each run read costs one request. 0 = the jobs are not read and only the finished-run costs (FinOps) feed the model. Default 10.
cfg.h.runners.model.thirdparty_labels: A job whose label starts with one of these names is a paid runner of another company, which GitHub does not bill (default: blacksmith, buildjet, namespace-profile, depot, warpbuild, ubicloud, runs-on, actuated, cirrus-runners, codspeed). Changing the list replaces it.
cfg.h.runners.model.large_labels: Names or patterns (with * and ?) of the labels of your own larger-runner groups, for example my-big-*. The labels of GitHub's larger runners (with -8-cores, large, xlarge) are always known. Empty by default.
cfg.h.runners.model.self_labels: Labels, besides self-hosted, that also mean a runner of your own (for example the name of a group of your runners). Empty by default.
cfg.h.runners.model.thirdparty_usd_per_m: What a minute of a paid third-party runner costs you, in dollars. 0 (default) = unknown: the minutes are counted but no cost is shown for them.
cfg.h.runners.model.queue_warn_minutes: A job that has waited this long for a self-hosted runner is listed; if no runner that is online has its labels, it is an alert. Default 20.
cfg.h.runners.model.runaway_runs_per_hou: A workflow with at least this many runs started in the last hour is shown as firing itself (pull requests do not count by default). The monitor only sees the runs it samples per repository, so keep this at or below the runs per repository. 0 = off. Default 20.
cfg.h.runners.model.runaway_ignore_event: Events that never count towards a workflow firing itself. Default: pull_request, pull_request_target.
cfg.h.runners.model.alerts: On (default, only while the model is on): a workflow that fires itself and a job that waits for a self-hosted runner that is offline or missing appear in the Alerts tab. Off = they are only shown in the Advanced tab.
cfg.h.runners.model.alert_level: Level of the alerts of the model: info, warning (default) or error.
cfg.h.runs_per_repo: Runs read for each hot repository.
cfg.h.savings.feeds.enabled: Before a quiet repository is read with the API, the newest commit of its default branch is asked from a source that costs no allowance (the public Atom feed or git ls-remote). If nothing was pushed since the last full read, the repository is left as it is. Public repositories only; a private one, an error or an odd answer means it is read with the API as always. Only GET requests to github.com leave the computer.
cfg.h.savings.feeds.max_age_minutes: A safety net: a repository whose newest commit has not changed is still read in full after this many minutes.
cfg.h.savings.feeds.method: atom: the Atom feed of the commits; git: git ls-remote (needs git installed); auto: the feed and, if it does not answer, git.
cfg.h.savings.webhook_first: While the incoming webhook is alive (it delivered an event lately), a quiet repository is not read on its slow turn: GitHub says when something happens. It is still read in full from time to time. Without a live webhook nothing changes. A run that starts without a push is seen at the next full read.
cfg.h.savings.webhook_full_minutes: A safety net: even with a live webhook, a quiet repository is read in full after this many minutes.
cfg.h.savings.webhook_window_minutes: Minutes after the last event during which the webhook is trusted to tell about changes.
cfg.h.score.alert.drop_points: Points the score must fall, against the window before, to raise the alert.
cfg.h.score.alert.enabled: Raises an alert in the panel when the score falls by the points below or to a lower letter.
cfg.h.score.alert.notify_external: Also sends the score alert through the external notification channels. Off by default.
cfg.h.score.calibrating_hours: An account watched for less time than this shows no score yet.
cfg.h.score.enabled: Switches the account score (number, letter and trend) on or off.
cfg.h.score.grades.A: From this score the letter is A; it must be higher than the one for B.
cfg.h.score.grades.B: From this score the letter is B; it must be higher than the one for C.
cfg.h.score.grades.C: From this score the letter is C; it must be higher than the one for D.
cfg.h.score.grades.D: From this score the letter is D; below it the letter is E.
cfg.h.score.min_coverage: The parts of the score that have data must weigh at least this share of the total.
cfg.h.score.min_runs: With fewer finished runs in the window the score says there is not enough data.
cfg.h.score.trend_flat: A change smaller than this many points counts as flat.
cfg.h.score.weights.collaboration: Share of the score given to the time collaboration items take to be resolved.
cfg.h.score.weights.recovery: Share of the score given to the time a failing workflow takes to recover.
cfg.h.score.weights.reliability: Share of the score given to the success rate of the CI.
cfg.h.score.weights.security: Share of the score given to what the Security sentinel finds open. It only counts while that sentinel is on.
cfg.h.score.weights.speed: Share of the score given to the 95th percentile of the duration of the successful runs.
cfg.h.score.window_days: Days of runs the score looks at; the window of the same length before it gives the trend.
cfg.h.sentinel.a2_full_sample_unknown: Show unknown instead of green when an old workflow may be hidden beyond the sample.
cfg.h.sentinel.a2_resolve_max_calls_per_: Extra lookups per cycle to settle an unknown workflow; 0 never asks.
cfg.h.sentinel.a2_resolve_ttl_seconds: How long an answer of that lookup is kept.
cfg.h.sentinel.alerts_hot_seconds: Time between two reads of the security alerts of hot repositories.
cfg.h.sentinel.audit_files.reconciliatio: Name pattern of the reconciliation files in the audit folder.
cfg.h.sentinel.audit_files.rounds: Name pattern of the rounds files.
cfg.h.sentinel.audit_files.rounds_extra: Name pattern of the extra rounds files.
cfg.h.sentinel.bots_apart: Off (default). On: pull requests of accounts that GitHub itself calls bots (type Bot, not a guess from the name) are not counted as the work of a person: A4 counts them apart and the check of old pull requests waiting for a person leaves them out.
cfg.h.sentinel.budget_per_hour: Most API calls the sentinel makes in an hour.
cfg.h.sentinel.candidate_days: Days with unpublished changes before a repository is a release candidate.
cfg.h.sentinel.candidate_min_entries: Changelog entries needed to be a candidate.
cfg.h.sentinel.ci_red_audit_copy: Also copies ci_red.json into the audit folder.
cfg.h.sentinel.ci_red_file: Where ci_red.json is written; empty is the ai/ folder of the monitor, off writes none.
cfg.h.sentinel.dependency_bots: One per line: dependabot and renovate by default. Their pull requests are the dependency updates of A4, and a repository with a Renovate configuration counts as covered like one with dependabot.yml.
cfg.h.sentinel.enabled: Switches the whole sentinel (alerts, releases, readiness) on or off.
cfg.h.sentinel.hot_hours: A repository is hot for the sentinel this long after a push.
cfg.h.sentinel.hygiene.community_fallbac: A file missing in a repository still counts when the community profile of GitHub or the .github repository of the account provides it. Costs one extra request per repository every hygiene period.
cfg.h.sentinel.hygiene.ruleset_mode: name: a ruleset with one of the names below must be ACTIVE (the old rule). effective: the default branch counts as protected when GitHub reports a rule or a protection for it, whatever the ruleset is called (needs no admin rights). off: not checked.
cfg.h.sentinel.hygiene.ruleset_names: One per line. A name or a pattern with * (for example main-*); used when the check is set to name. Default: protect-main.
cfg.h.sentinel.hygiene.skip: One per line, from: ruleset, label, file, sha, allowed, schedule. A check that does not apply to your repositories is left out of the list of problems.
cfg.h.sentinel.hygiene_seconds: Time between two checks of repository rules, labels and files.
cfg.h.sentinel.max_calls_per_tick: Most API calls the sentinel makes in one cycle.
cfg.h.sentinel.min_rate_remaining: Below this allowance the sentinel waits.
cfg.h.sentinel.minutes_budget: Ceiling of Actions minutes per ecosystem; empty means no ceiling.
cfg.h.sentinel.minutes_budget_period: Window over which the minutes of each ecosystem are counted.
cfg.h.sentinel.pending_sign_hours: A green build waiting this long for its signature is reported.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.enabled: Switches release readiness, ecosystem health and pins on or off.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.min_coverage: An ecosystem gets a score only when this share of its repositories has data.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.pins.max_depth: Folder levels searched for lock files.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.pins.refresh_se: Time between two readings of the pinned versions.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.pins.sources: Where the pins live, as a JSON list; empty reads nothing.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.warn_below: The report warns about an ecosystem whose score is below this.
cfg.h.sentinel.require_verified_signatur: A signature counts only when it verifies against the public key of the ecosystem.
cfg.h.sentinel.required_files: Files every repository must have; one group per line, alternatives separated by ;.
cfg.h.sentinel.skip_candidate_prefixes: Repositories starting with these prefixes are never proposed for a release.
cfg.h.sentinel.stale_pr_days: A pull request open this long is reported as stale.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.budget_share: Share of the sentinel budget these checks may use.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.checks.release_as: Off (default): a release with no files at all is reported. On for projects that publish to a package registry and only tag on GitHub.
On (default): a release without a .sha256 file or SHA256SUMS is reported. Off for projects that do not publish checksums.
On (default): a release without a .sig file is reported. Off for projects that do not sign their files.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.checks.tag_vs_ver: One per line, for example cli-. A tag such as cli-v1.2.0 is compared with the manifest as v1.2.0; without a prefix it is not compared at all.
On: 2026.11.16-beta.2 and 2026.11.16 are compared as 2026.11.16. For calendar versions with several betas on one day.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.enabled: Switches all the checks of the Actions and releases surface on or off.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.local_seconds: Time between two scans of the local clones.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.max_repos_per_tic: Repositories read from GitHub in one cycle.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.min_rate_factor: Starts only when the allowance left is this many times the pause limit.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.refresh_seconds: Time between two readings of GitHub data of each repository.
cfg.h.sentinel.workers: Requests the sentinel makes at the same time.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.enabled: Switches the sentinel of issues and pull requests on or off (off by default).
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.max_repos_per_tic: How many repositories one round reads (two requests each): the rest wait for the next round.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.min_rate_remainin: The sentinel stops while the GitHub allowance is below this.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.refresh_seconds: Time between two rounds of the Collab sentinel.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.repos: all, or a list of repositories, or the ecosystems to watch.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.ignore_labe: An issue or pull request with one of these labels (put by a person on GitHub) raises no alert; one per line.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.issue_criti: An open issue with one of these labels is always flagged; one per line.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.issue_stale: An open issue with no activity for this long is flagged.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.pr_conflict: A pull request with conflicts for this long is flagged.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.pr_draft_ma: A draft pull request open for this long is flagged.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.pr_review_p: A pull request with a requested review that has waited this long is flagged.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.watch_exter: Also flags issues from people outside the team that nobody has answered after a day.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.search_api: Off: the Collab sentinel reads two lists for each repository. On: it asks the open issues and pull requests of the whole account in a few calls of the Search API (its own allowance, 30 a minute, which the REST allowance does not pay), then reads only the conflicts of the pull requests that changed. The alerts are the same in both ways; if the Search API fails the round reads each repository as before. A pull request found this way does not say whether a review was requested.
cfg.h.sentinels.security.enabled: Reads, without writing anything, what GitHub says is open or missing about security in each repository. Off by default.
cfg.h.sentinels.security.max_repos_per_t: At most this many repositories are read in one round (up to seven calls each, most of them answered without using allowance).
cfg.h.sentinels.security.deadline_s: Seconds. A round stops starting new repositories when this time has passed; the ones not reached keep waiting (the oldest read goes first next round) and are listed by name as not checked instead of counting as zero alerts. 0 = no ceiling.
cfg.h.sentinels.security.min_rate_remain: The sentinel pauses while the GitHub allowance left is below this.
cfg.h.sentinels.security.refresh_seconds: Seconds between two rounds of the Security sentinel.
cfg.h.sentinels.security.repos: All the repositories, or the ones of some ecosystems, or a list of names.
Raises a warning when the default branch of a repository has no protection. A repository where the login may not read it is listed as unreadable, not as a finding.
cfg.h.sentinels.security.signals.code_sc: Raises an alert for the open code scanning alerts of a repository.
Only the alerts at this severity or above count (low, medium, high, critical).
cfg.h.sentinels.security.signals.codeown: Raises a notice when a repository has no CODEOWNERS file. Off by default: many repositories do not want one.
cfg.h.sentinels.security.signals.dependa: Raises an alert for the open Dependabot alerts of a repository.
Only the alerts at this severity or above count (low, medium, high, critical).
Raises a critical alert for every open secret scanning alert: a secret found by GitHub is a secret that is out.
cfg.h.sentinels.security.signals.workflo: Raises a warning when the workflows of a repository get write permission by default.
cfg.h.session_guard: The page asks for a fresh token right before it saves a setting or confirms an action, so another page in your browser cannot do it for you.
cfg.h.show_unclassified: Repositories that no ecosystem claims appear in an automatic group Unclassified instead of disappearing (only with all ecosystems).
cfg.h.signed_dir: Folder with the local records of signing and batches.
cfg.h.sound.cooldown_seconds: Minimum time between two sounds, so a burst of failures sounds once. 0 = no pause.
cfg.h.sound.enabled: Main switch of the "bing bing" (two short tones) of the page. The chip "Sound" of the bar at the foot mutes it in this browser.
cfg.h.sound.on_connection_lost: Sounds once when the connection to GitHub goes from online to offline. It also sounds once when this page loses the connection with the monitor itself (no answer for over a minute) and the bar turns red; it respects the mute chip, the cooldown and the browser's sound block.
cfg.h.sound.on_new_red: Sounds when a failure that was not there before appears (not for the ones already open and not at every refresh).
cfg.h.sound.server_beep: Off by default. The "bing bing" of the page only sounds while a page is open in a browser that has had one click (the notice "Sound blocked" says so). With this switch the monitor itself sounds on this computer (Windows tones, macOS system sounds, Linux canberra or the terminal bell) even when no page is open or the browser blocks sound, with one pattern for each kind of event (a new red, a lost connection, the live view back, a warning, a solved one, a report, a lesson, a security alert, a stuck run, a score drop, a notice), by the same switches as the page and respecting the quiet hours. It never uses the network and a missing program is not an error.
cfg.h.sound.volume: Volume of the tones of the page, from 1 to 100 (moderate by default). Use the button "Test sound" in This browser to hear it.
cfg.h.stuck_minutes: A run that lasts longer than this is shown as stuck.
cfg.h.targets_file: JSON file with the catalogue of build targets.
cfg.h.tools_dir: Folder of your local signing tools; empty if you have none.
cfg.h.tui.refresh_seconds: Time between two redraws of the terminal view.
cfg.h.ui.alerts_sort: How the list of the Alerts tab is sorted for a person who has not chosen another order: server (as the monitor sends them, the default), severity, streak, class, age, newest, repo, origin or state. Class puts the real alerts (error or critical) before the ones to watch (warning or info). Each person can change it with the list above the alerts and the monitor remembers it for them (in the team mode on the server, otherwise in the browser).
cfg.h.ui.now_sort: How the section Happening now of the first tab is sorted for a person who has not chosen another order: ecosystem (the default, with a heading for each one), severity, age, newest, repo, event or state. Each person can change it with the list above the section and the monitor remembers it for them (in the team mode on the server, otherwise in the browser).
cfg.h.ui.orientation: auto follows the window (a window taller than wide stacks the panels); portrait or landscape forces it. Useful for a monitor turned 90 degrees or a TV. The address can force it for one window: ?orient=portrait.
cfg.h.ui.rotate_seconds: 0 = no rotation. With more than one tab on a screen, the page turns through them by itself every this many seconds (for a screen nobody touches). ?rotate=30 does it for one window.
cfg.h.ui.screen1_orientation: auto = the general orientation above; portrait or landscape forces it on /screen/1 only.
cfg.h.ui.screen1_tabs: Tabs that /screen/1 shows, separated by commas, from: now, al, charts, sent, sci, scol, ssec, team, fleet, repos, rep, trep, les, hist, cfg (all, lite: now, charts, repos, hist, cfg). Empty = all tabs. Open http://this-computer:8765/screen/1 on that monitor.
cfg.h.ui.screen2_orientation: auto = the general orientation above; portrait or landscape forces it on /screen/2 only.
cfg.h.ui.screen2_tabs: Tabs that /screen/2 shows, separated by commas, from: now, al, charts, sent, sci, scol, ssec, team, fleet, repos, rep, trep, les, hist, cfg (all, lite: now, charts, repos, hist, cfg). Empty = all tabs. Open http://this-computer:8765/screen/2 on that monitor.
cfg.h.ui.screen3_orientation: auto = the general orientation above; portrait or landscape forces it on /screen/3 only.
cfg.h.ui.screen3_tabs: Tabs that /screen/3 shows, separated by commas, from: now, al, charts, sent, sci, scol, ssec, team, fleet, repos, rep, trep, les, hist, cfg (all, lite: now, charts, repos, hist, cfg). Empty = all tabs. Open http://this-computer:8765/screen/3 on that monitor.
cfg.h.updates.check: One read-only request a day to the public releases page, through your own gh. It never downloads or installs anything and sends nothing about you.
cfg.h.watchdog_max_abandoned: A call to GitHub that does not answer in time is given up on, but its thread can stay alive. With this many of them still alive the monitor starts no new call to GitHub and its deep health check says it is degraded, instead of piling up threads and connections. 0 means no limit.
cfg.h.watchdog_minutes: If one refresh cycle of the monitor runs longer than this, the watchdog writes where every thread is to the log and starts the cycle again in a new thread. 0 switches the watchdog off.
cfg.h.webhook.enabled: Opens the receiver on 127.0.0.1; every request needs a valid signature.
cfg.h.webhook.live_events_keep: The newest events held in memory.
cfg.h.webhook.max_bad_per_minute: Per minute. More are refused with 429. They never use up the allowance of the deliveries that carry a good signature.
cfg.h.webhook.max_verified_per_minute: Per minute. More are refused with 429, even with a good signature.
cfg.h.webhook.reject_stale: Off by default. A signed workflow event whose own time is older than the time deliveries are remembered is answered and not acted on (a captured delivery sent again much later).
cfg.h.webhook.persist_deliveries: On by default. The memory of deliveries is kept in a file of the data folder (mode 0600, bounded), so a restart does not make a captured delivery valid again.
cfg.h.webhook.max_per_minute: Per minute. More are answered but ignored.
cfg.h.webhook.record_events: Use workflow_run and workflow_job events to update the runs without reading GitHub.
cfg.h.webhook.replay_seconds: A delivery that was already accepted is refused again during this time (protection against a captured request sent twice).
cfg.h.webhook.secret_env: The NAME of the variable that holds the shared secret (32 characters or more in its value). The secret is never written in the configuration, shown or logged.
cfg.h.webhook.signing_state: Whether the secret reached the monitor through its environment variable and is long enough; it is never shown here.
cfg.h.weight: Points taken off the health score of an ecosystem for each case.
cfg.h.workspace_root: Folder that holds your local clones.

doctor.f.backend: The plain file (permissions 600) is the weakest store: a backup of your home folder copies it. Prefer the store of the system (set github_token.store to system) or keep using your own gh login.
doctor.f.credential: Two or more accounts read GitHub with the same personal access token (the detail shows a short fingerprint and the accounts, never the token): one rate limit and one point of failure for all of them, and a leak exposes every account. Give each account its own token.
doctor.f.degraded: Some parts failed and the monitor kept running without them (the number and the origin are shown). Look at the log; if the number keeps growing, restart and report it.
doctor.f.docker: Not needed unless you want the container example.
doctor.f.exposure: The network mode is on: every request needs the access token. Turn listen.network off if you did not mean it.
doctor.f.folder: Move the monitor to a folder where you can write.
doctor.f.gh: Install gh with one of these commands.
doctor.f.github_app: The App is turned on but something is missing: the program openssl, the key file or its permissions (the key must be readable only by you). Until then the reads use your token.
doctor.f.layout: Files of the old flat layout are still next to the new ones. The monitor does not use them. Run: python tools/migrate_layout.py (a dry run), then add --apply to move them out of the way; your configuration and data stay where they are.
doctor.f.login: Log in once with gh. The monitor keeps no token unless you switch that on in Advanced.
doctor.f.network: GitHub cannot be reached; check the connection or the proxy.
doctor.f.port: Both ports are busy; start with another one.
doctor.f.python: Install a newer Python from python.org.
doctor.f.quota: The allowance is low or unreadable; wait for it to renew.
doctor.f.retention: The events of an account are bigger than the warning limit, or this monitor runs as a service and its configuration has no retention block. Set the retention settings (days to keep, mode) in the settings page, tab Folders and files, or in actions_monitor.json.
doctor.f.risks: network_all = listening on every interface (use one private address); execute_network = AI actions may run while the monitor is reachable from the network; token_file = the own token sits in a plain file; act_network = act can run while the monitor is reachable from the network. Turn one of the two options off.
doctor.f.storage: The database of an account is missing, damaged or newer than this version. Make a backup first: python tools/backup_storage.py backup FILE.zip --backend sqlite. To move data between files and SQLite use python tools/migrate_storage.py (a dry run first).
doctor.f.targets: Only the neutral example is used; create your own copies.
doctor.f.textual: Only for the interactive terminal application.
doctor.f.timezone: The zone is not recognised on this computer, so the times are shown in UTC. Use "local", "utc" or an IANA name such as Europe/Madrid in Settings (Interface), or fix MONITOR_TIMEZONE.
doctor.f.token: Turn session_guard back on in the settings.

Turn listen.network off, start the monitor (it then listens on this computer only), open the page and create the administrator, then turn listen.network on and start it again.
mon.network_needs_admin_service: The network mode (listen.network) is on together with the team mode (auth.enabled), but there is no administrator yet and the monitor does not start. In a container the network mode cannot be turned off: create the first administrator once with `docker compose run --rm --entrypoint python monitor -m github_actions_monitor.security.auth_cli create-admin NAME` (it asks for the password), or set MONITOR_ADMIN_USER and MONITOR_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE, and start the service again.

cfg.h.chatops.allowed_channels: Slack channel ids (C... or G...) or Discord channel ids. Same rule as the teams.
cfg.h.chatops.allowed_teams: Slack team ids (T...) or Discord server ids. At least one of the three lists must be filled in: with none, no command runs. A list that has entries must contain the team, the channel or the user of the request.
cfg.h.chatops.allowed_users: Slack user ids (U... or W...) or Discord user ids. Same rule as the teams.
cfg.h.chatops.allowed_words: A subset of: help, status, alerts, red, queue, score. All of them only read. Remove the ones you do not want in the chat; the list can never be widened from here.
cfg.h.chatops.discord.enabled: Accept the interactions of your Discord app at POST /api/chatops/discord. Needs the public key of the app in the environment variable below.
cfg.h.chatops.discord.public_key_env: The NAME of the variable. The public key of the app (64 hexadecimal characters, from the Developer Portal) checks the Ed25519 signature of every interaction before anything is read.
cfg.h.chatops.discord.state: Whether a valid public key reached the monitor through its environment variable; it is never shown here.
cfg.h.chatops.enabled: Off by default. Master switch of the read only commands from a chat. Nothing runs until a platform is also switched on, its proof is in the environment and at least one list of allowed teams, channels or users is filled in. The commands only read: they never change GitHub, a setting or an action. See docs/CHATOPS.md.
cfg.h.chatops.max_age_seconds: A request older than this (or from the future) is refused even with a good signature. Five minutes at most.
cfg.h.chatops.max_rows: Most lines that a list (open alerts, red workflows) shows in the chat.
cfg.h.chatops.rate_per_channel_per_minut: More commands than this in one channel in a minute get a short refusal.
cfg.h.chatops.rate_per_minute: Ceiling for all the commands of a platform in a minute.
cfg.h.chatops.rate_per_user_per_minute: More commands than this from one person in a minute get a short refusal.
cfg.h.chatops.show_repo_names: all = every name, private repositories included (their names reach every channel and user of the lists, which is why the lists are required and must all match); public = a private repository appears as private-N and its workflows are not named; none = repo-N for all. Texts that come from GitHub are always cleaned and cut.
cfg.h.chatops.links: Add the address of the repository (https://<host>/<owner>/<repository>) to the lines of alerts and red workflows, only when its name is shown as it is. It is the only link an answer ever carries.
cfg.h.chatops.slack.enabled: Accept the slash command of your Slack app at POST /api/chatops/slack. Needs the signing secret in the environment variable below.
cfg.h.chatops.slack.signing_secret_env: The NAME of the variable, never the secret itself. Every request is checked with the signature v0 (HMAC-SHA256 of the time and the body, at most five minutes old) before anything of it is read.
cfg.h.chatops.slack.state: Whether the secret reached the monitor through its environment variable (at least 16 characters); it is never shown here.
chatops.busy: The monitor is busy. Try again in a moment.

chatops.score_off: The score is off or still being calibrated.

cfg.f.sampling.default_branch_probe: Second look at the default branch
cfg.h.sampling.default_branch_probe: When the list of runs of a repository is full, one more request asks for the pushes to its default branch (pull requests left out), so the runs that decide red on main are not pushed out by pull requests and schedules. Costs one request per full repository per read; off by default.
cfg.h.sampling.min_coverage_minutes: A full list of runs that reaches back less than this many minutes is marked low coverage instead of looking complete. 0 turns the mark off.
cfg.h.sampling.api_budget_per_hour: Most requests for run lists in one hour (0 = no budget). Past it, repositories with a red workflow are read first and the rest wait, and the page says so.
cfg.f.sentinel.a2_resolve_batch_min: A2 lookups in one request from
cfg.h.sentinel.a2_resolve_batch_min: A repository with at least this many workflows to look up is asked once for its newest completed runs of the default branch and all of them are settled together; the others go one by one. 0 always asks one by one.
cfg.h.sentinel.a2_resolve_batch_pages: How many pages of 100 runs that single request may read (each page is one call).
ui.sampling_low: {n} repositories have low coverage: their list of runs reaches back only a few minutes, so an older failure may not be seen. Raise the runs per repository or turn on the second look.
ui.sampling_estimate: About {est} requests per hour for {n} repositories ({used} used in the last hour); the allowance of GitHub is 5,000 per hour.
ui.sampling_waiting: Request budget spent: {n} repositories wait for the next hour, the ones with red are read first.
