cfg.h.ci.group.reusable: Off by default. On: red workflows that call the same reusable workflow have one cause; the red list shows a group line for it and the notification of the new reds says it once with the number affected instead of once for each. No red row is hidden.
cfg.f.ci.group.min: Workflows needed for a shared cause
cfg.h.ci.group.min: A reusable workflow is named as a shared cause from this many red workflows (default 2).
cfg.f.ci.failed_jobs.enabled: Show which jobs of a red run failed
cfg.h.ci.failed_jobs.enabled: Off by default. On: for each red run the monitor reads its jobs once (one call, a few runs per cycle) and the red row says which jobs failed, grouped by platform, so a workflow with many jobs does not just say red.
cfg.h.ci.failed_jobs.max_per_cycle: The most red runs whose jobs are read in one cycle (one call each, default 4). The answer is kept while the run stays the same.
cfg.h.ci.failed_jobs.group_by: auto (default): the system in the name of the job (ubuntu, windows, macos...), else the first parameter of the matrix, else the part before the slash. platform, matrix and prefix force one of those.
cfg.f.ci.stuck.learned: Learn the limit of each workflow
cfg.h.ci.stuck.learned: Off by default: one limit (the one above) for every workflow. On: a workflow with enough finished runs gets the limit its own runs suggest (a percentile of their durations times a margin, between the minimum and the maximum below), so a build of six hours is not stuck at hour two.
cfg.h.ci.stuck.percentile: Which long duration of a workflow counts as normal when the limit is learned (default 95).
cfg.h.ci.stuck.margin: The learned limit is that duration times this number (default 2).
cfg.h.ci.stuck.min_samples: A workflow with fewer successful finished runs than this keeps the common limit (default 3).
cfg.h.ci.stuck.min_minutes: A learned limit is never lower than this, so a workflow that usually takes one minute is not stuck after two (default 30).
cfg.h.ci.stuck.max_minutes: A learned limit is never higher than this, so a run that really hangs is still caught (default 720 = 12 hours).
cfg.f.ci.stuck.queue_minutes: Limit for a run waiting for a runner
cfg.h.ci.stuck.queue_minutes: A run that has not started because it waits for a runner may wait this long before it counts as stuck. 0 (default) uses the same limit as a running build.
cfg.f.ci.stuck.awaiting_stuck: A run waiting for approval can be stuck
cfg.h.ci.stuck.awaiting_stuck: On by default (as before). Off: a run held for an approval is never reported as stuck, only shown as waiting for approval.
cfg.f.ci.stuck.ghost_enabled: Tell apart runs queued for days
cfg.h.ci.stuck.ghost_enabled: On by default. A run that has been in the queue for more than the days below is not waiting for a runner any more (GitHub never starts it): it is not counted as queued or stuck and gives no red or stuck alarm; it is shown apart so that it can be cancelled. Off: it is treated like any other queued run.
cfg.f.ci.stuck.ghost_days: Days in the queue until a run is a ghost
cfg.h.ci.stuck.ghost_days: Default 7. A queued run (first attempt) older than this many days is a ghost queue: it only produces an information notice. Used only while the switch above is on.
cfg.h.ci.stuck.workflow_minutes: Entries like build.yml=420 (workflow file or name, * allowed, then the limit in minutes). It wins over the learned limit and over the runner limit. Empty by default.
cfg.h.ci.stuck.runner_minutes: Entries like self-hosted=720 (label of the runner, * allowed, then the limit in minutes), for jobs on slow or shared machines. Needs one extra read per queued run (at most 10 per cycle). Empty by default.
ui.stuck_why_ghost: queued for days; GitHub does not start it
ui.n_ghost: {n} queued for more than {days} days (probably never start; not stuck, not queued)
ui.n_inactive: {n} failed workflows no longer count as red (inactive, or the failure is older than the red age)
ui.n_dormant: {n} dormant and {m} inactive repositories (no recent activity)

evt.silence_review: A silence is due for review: {pattern} ({reason}, review by {date})
ui.cfg_b_flow_digest: Hourly summary when there are many
cfg.f.alerts.silences_expire_days: Days after the review date when a silence expires
cfg.h.alerts.silences: One entry per line: repository:workflow:branch;reason;review date (for example demo-repo:nightly.yml:*;known flaky test;2027-03-01). Every part but the repository may be left out or be *, and * matches any text. A matching alert is shown as silenced and nobody is notified; on the review date one reminder is announced and the silence keeps working until you remove it. Empty by default. It only silences the notices of a red or stuck workflow: a new security alert (secret scanning, CodeQL, Dependabot), a required check in red, a pending signature or a release notice of that repository is always announced, and the Alerts tab never shows it as silenced.
cfg.h.alerts.silences_expire_days: 0 (the default) = a silence by pattern never expires and keeps working after its review date. With a number, a silence stops working that many days after its review date and its alerts are announced again; a silence without a review date never expires. The Alerts signals list the silences past their date, expired or without a date.
cfg.h.alerts.service.enabled: Off by default. On: a workflow that only runs on a schedule or by hand, and fails now and then, is announced only after it failed several times in a row (or too often), once, and cleared once, instead of alerting in a loop. It still shows red in the lists.
cfg.f.alerts.service.failures: Failures in a row before it alerts
cfg.h.alerts.service.failures: A service-class workflow is announced after this many failures in a row (default 3).
cfg.f.alerts.service.rate_percent: Or when this share of its last runs failed
cfg.h.alerts.service.rate_percent: 0 (default) turns it off. Otherwise a service-class workflow whose last runs (at least 4 of the last 10) failed at this rate or more is announced even without a streak.
cfg.f.alerts.service.workflows: More workflows of the service class
cfg.h.alerts.service.workflows: Entries like demo-repo:nightly.yml (repository:workflow, * allowed) for workflows that should be treated as services even though they also run on push. Empty by default.
cfg.f.alerts.group.by_commit: Group new reds of the same commit
cfg.h.alerts.group.by_commit: Off by default. On: when several workflows of one repository turn red on the same commit, ONE notification lists them instead of one message each. The lists and the Alerts tab are not changed.
cfg.h.alerts.group.min: Reds of one commit are grouped from this many workflows (default 3).
cfg.h.alerts.digest.minutes: 0 (default) turns it off. Otherwise, once more notifications than the threshold below were sent in the last hour, the rest are held back and told as ONE summary every this many minutes (60 = hourly). The held events stay in the events feed.
cfg.h.alerts.digest.threshold: This many notifications an hour are sent one by one; beyond it they are summarised (default 10).
cfg.f.lint.source: Where the workflow files are read
cfg.h.lint.source: clone (default): only the local clones. auto: also, for the repositories without a clone, the folder .github/workflows through the GitHub API (one call for the list and one for each file that changed; a file whose SHA did not change is never read again). sparse: a sparse clone of depth 1 that brings only .github. Use auto or sparse when cloning every repository is not an option. What cannot be read is shown as not evaluable, with the reason.
cfg.h.lint.api.refresh_seconds: Seconds between two readings of the same repository through the API (default 21600, six hours). The list of files is read again; only the files whose SHA changed are downloaded.
cfg.f.lint.api.max_calls_per_tick: API calls per cycle for workflow files
cfg.h.lint.api.max_calls_per_tick: Upper limit of the calls of one cycle spent on reading workflow files without a clone (default 20). It also stays inside the hourly budget of the Sentinel and stops while the allowance is low; the repositories that did not get their turn show as waiting.
cfg.h.lint.api.max_files_per_repo: A repository with more workflow files than this is read in part and says so (default 40, at most 100).
cfg.h.lint.sparse.refresh_seconds: Seconds between two refreshes of the sparse clone of a repository (default 21600). Only .github is fetched, with depth 1, in a background thread.
cfg.h.lint.sparse.max_repos_per_tick: How many repositories get their sparse clone made or refreshed in one cycle (default 2, at most 20). A clone of depth 1 without file contents is small, but git can take a minute.
ui.a13_cov: Read from: {clone} local clones, {sparse} sparse clones, {api} through the GitHub API.
ui.a13_cov_partial: {n} read only in part (call budget or file limit).
ui.a13_cov_cannot: Through the API these cannot be checked: stacks, dependabot.yml, manifest and CHANGELOG (they need a clone).
ui.ai_preset_examples: The example models are only examples and may be out of date: load the real list of the provider below.
lint.reason.sso: the token is not authorised for the organization (SSO)
lint.reason.forbidden: the token lacks a scope or a permission
lint.help_remote: Read the workflow files of a repository from GitHub (no clone); can be repeated.
doctor.t.access: The login can read the account or organization
doctor.f.access: A 403 or a 404 on an organization usually means one of these: the token is not authorised for its SAML single sign-on (authorise it under Configure SSO on the token page), it lacks the scope repo or read:org (or, for a fine-grained token, a read permission), or the repositories are private and the login cannot see them. The detail names which one.
doctor.t.estimate: The reads an hour fit the allowance
doctor.f.estimate: With this many repositories the monitor would use a large part of the allowance of the token (estimate, with the current settings). Raise cold_refresh_seconds, lower the hot repositories, turn on Low mode, or read with a GitHub App (see QUOTA.md and ORGANIZATIONS.md).
cfg.h.pagination.workflow_pages: A repository can have hundreds of workflows. While a page of 100 is full, the next one is read, up to this many pages; a repository with fewer than 100 costs no extra request. If something is still left out the page says how many were seen of how many exist.
cfg.h.pagination.job_pages: A matrix can start more than 100 jobs in one run. While a page of 100 is full, the next one is read, up to this many pages. If jobs are still left out, the run says "seen N of M".
cfg.f.pagination.collab_pages: Pages of issues and pull requests per repository
cfg.h.ai.catalog.enabled: Off: the list of models is read only when you ask for it (the button below or `monitor_cli.py ai models --refresh`). On: the monitor also keeps the list and warns when the configured model no longer appears in it (retired or renamed). It is one read-only request to your provider, with no data of your repositories; the key is read from its environment variable.
cfg.h.ai.catalog.fit_context: Off: the input limit is the value you set. On: when the context window of the model is known (from the provider or typed in the table) the input is cut to about half of it, never above your limit. A model whose window is unknown keeps your limit.
cfg.h.ai.catalog.max_requests_per_day: The most requests to the list of models of the provider in a day, whoever asks (the check, the button, the command). At the cap the list kept is shown and nothing more is asked.
cfg.h.ai.catalog.ttl_minutes: How long the list kept stays valid before the monitor reads it again (only when the check above is on).
cfg.h.ai.cost_limit_daily: 0 = no limit. Only the calls whose prices are known (the table of models) are added up, in the unit of those prices. When it is reached no model is called until tomorrow. A call of a model without prices counts for the calls only, so the total is a lower bound. It also counts the calls of the active notice, which keeps its own limits per hour as well. The notice used to be outside these limits: if it needs more than this total allows, raise the total.
cfg.h.ai.fallback: An ordered list `provider=model, provider=model` (provider: a preset such as `openai` or `ollama`, or a protocol). They are tried in order when the main model fails (any error, a refused key, a model that does not exist, the quota), has been retired from the list of the provider or has spent its budget. Empty: no fallback, as before.
cfg.h.ai.fallback_after_seconds: 0 uses the general time limit. With a fallback, a model that does not answer within this many seconds is given up and the next one is tried (the time counts every network operation, not the whole call).
cfg.h.ai.fallback_max_attempts: Counts the main model too: 1 turns the chain off, 5 is the most. There is never a loop, a model is tried once and an answer already kept costs nothing.
cfg.h.ai.fallback_cloud_allowed: Names (the preset or the protocol written in the list of fallbacks, for example openai) of the providers that are NOT on this computer and may receive the text of a failed build when the main model fails. Empty by default: a provider on the internet is never tried as a fallback until you write its name here. Every time the chain goes from this computer to the internet it is written in the log of actions and a notice is sent.
cfg.h.ai.model_cost_limit_daily: 0 = no limit. The most estimated cost one model may add up in a day; the figure typed for a model in the table wins. A model that reaches it is skipped (the fallback answers, or nobody does). It also counts the calls of the active notice, which keeps its own limits per hour as well. The notice used to be outside these limits: if it needs more than this total allows, raise the total.
cfg.h.ai.model_daily_limit: 0 = no limit. Each model may be called this many times a day; the figure typed for a model in the table wins. A model that has spent its calls is skipped: the fallback answers, or nobody does. The limit is never jumped. It also counts the calls of the active notice, which keeps its own limits per hour as well. The notice used to be outside these limits: if it needs more than this total allows, raise the total.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.alert.max_input_chars: The most characters sent to the model for alert. 0 uses the general input limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.alert.max_output_chars: The most characters kept from the answer for alert. 0 uses the general output limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.alert.model: The model for alert. Empty: the general model, and everything works as before. Pick the name from the list of the provider (block *Models and data per model*).
cfg.h.ai.tasks.alert.provider: A preset (`openai`, `ollama`...) or a protocol (`ollama`, `anthropic`, `openai-compatible`) to use for alert. Empty: the general provider. It only counts together with a model. Not used for the active notice: its provider is always the one you confirmed for it, and only its model can change.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.alert.timeout_seconds: The longest wait for the model for alert, in seconds. 0 uses the general time limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.build.max_input_chars: The most characters sent to the model for build. 0 uses the general input limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.build.max_output_chars: The most characters kept from the answer for build. 0 uses the general output limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.build.model: The model for build. Empty: the general model, and everything works as before. Pick the name from the list of the provider (block *Models and data per model*).
cfg.h.ai.tasks.build.provider: A preset (`openai`, `ollama`...) or a protocol (`ollama`, `anthropic`, `openai-compatible`) to use for build. Empty: the general provider. It only counts together with a model.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.build.timeout_seconds: The longest wait for the model for build, in seconds. 0 uses the general time limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.codeql.max_input_chars: The most characters sent to the model for CodeQL. 0 uses the general input limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.codeql.max_output_chars: The most characters kept from the answer for CodeQL. 0 uses the general output limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.codeql.model: The model for CodeQL. Empty: the general model, and everything works as before. Pick the name from the list of the provider (block *Models and data per model*).
cfg.h.ai.tasks.codeql.provider: A preset (`openai`, `ollama`...) or a protocol (`ollama`, `anthropic`, `openai-compatible`) to use for CodeQL. Empty: the general provider. It only counts together with a model.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.codeql.timeout_seconds: The longest wait for the model for CodeQL, in seconds. 0 uses the general time limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.diagnose.max_input_chars: The most characters sent to the model for diagnosis. 0 uses the general input limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.diagnose.max_output_chars: The most characters kept from the answer for diagnosis. 0 uses the general output limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.diagnose.model: The model for diagnosis. Empty: the general model, and everything works as before. Pick the name from the list of the provider (block *Models and data per model*).
cfg.h.ai.tasks.diagnose.provider: A preset (`openai`, `ollama`...) or a protocol (`ollama`, `anthropic`, `openai-compatible`) to use for diagnosis. Empty: the general provider. It only counts together with a model.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.diagnose.timeout_seconds: The longest wait for the model for diagnosis, in seconds. 0 uses the general time limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.report.max_input_chars: The most characters sent to the model for report. 0 uses the general input limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.report.max_output_chars: The most characters kept from the answer for report. 0 uses the general output limit.
cfg.h.ai.tasks.report.model: The model for report. Empty: the general model, and everything works as before. Pick the name from the list of the provider (block *Models and data per model*).
cfg.h.ai.tasks.report.provider: A preset (`openai`, `ollama`...) or a protocol (`ollama`, `anthropic`, `openai-compatible`) to use for report. Empty: the general provider. It only counts together with a model.

cfg.h.pagination.collab_pages: A repository can have hundreds of open issues and pull requests. If more exist, the Team tab says so.
cfg.h.pagination.cursor_pages: The alerts of Dependabot, code scanning and secret scanning reject ?page=; they hand out a cursor in the Link header. While the first page of 100 has a next one, this many more pages are read (only addresses of the API itself are followed). 0 = only the first page. If more exist, the list is marked as cut.

cfg.h.screens.enabled: Turns the wall screens on. Off: /screen/overview, /screen/now and /screen/sentinels answer 404. They only read what the monitor already holds; they never change anything and never call GitHub. Off by default.
cfg.h.screens.default_theme: inherit = the theme chosen for the whole product (the default). Or one fixed for all the wall screens: auto, light, dark, one of the sixteen themes or contrast (white on black, for a screen seen from far away). Each screen can have its own below. The address can change it for one window: ?theme=light.
cfg.h.screens.default_density: compact, normal or large type. ?density=large changes it for one window; ?scale=1.5 enlarges everything.
cfg.f.screens.refresh_seconds: Seconds between updates of a wall screen
cfg.h.screens.refresh_seconds: How often a wall screen asks the monitor for its data (5 to 120). It reads the monitor, never GitHub, so a short time costs no allowance. ?refresh=20 changes it for one window.
cfg.h.screens.rotate_seconds: Only in three-screens mode. 0 = no rotation. Above that, a window turns by itself through Overview, Right now and Sentinels every this many seconds (at least 5). ?rotate=30 does it for one window. For a single screen that turns and jumps to a new red, use the rotate mode.
cfg.h.screens.blink: Failures blink softly (less than twice a second, never a strobe). A window can only turn it off (?blink=off). A system that asks for less motion never blinks; the failure keeps a fixed glow.
cfg.f.screens.blink_calm_minutes: Minutes until a failure stops blinking
cfg.h.screens.blink_calm_minutes: A failure that nobody has attended to for this many minutes stops blinking and keeps a fixed glow, so a screen that is always on does not tire the eyes. 0 = it blinks until it is solved.
cfg.h.screens.sound: The same sounds as the page, one for each kind of event (a new failure, one solved, a lost connection, a serious alert, a warning), with the theme, volume and quiet hours of the sound settings. Off by default; a window also needs ?sound=on, and the browser may ask for a click first.
cfg.h.screens.burn_in_protection: Moves everything a few pixels once a minute so fixed elements do not mark a screen that is always on.
cfg.h.screens.night_dim: Dims the wall screens between the two hours below (the clock of the screen that shows them).
cfg.h.screens.night_dim_from_hour: Hour (0 to 23) at which the screens dim when Dim at night is on.
cfg.h.screens.night_dim_to_hour: Hour (0 to 23) at which the screens go back to normal brightness.
cfg.f.screens.group_map: Group map on the overview screen
cfg.h.screens.show_repo_names: all shows every name; public hides the names of private repositories (they appear as private-1, private-2...); none hides every name (repo-1, repo-2...). Use public or none for a screen that other people can see. The workflow names of hidden repositories are hidden too.
cfg.h.screens.group_map: On by default. The overview wall screen shows the map of the fleet by groups, with the same grouping as the Fleet view (fleet.group_by: ecosystem, label or state): one bar for each group with its repositories that are red, need attention, are in order or have no data. ui.scr_sen_lite: The lite edition has no sentinels
cfg.f.api.experimental_routes: Routes that are not frozen in /api/v1/
cfg.h.api.v1_enabled: auto (default): the read API is on when the monitor runs as a service (an account of the team mode, the Docker image, the systemd unit) and off for one person at one computer. on: always. off: never (the whole prefix answers 404). When on, every read route is also served under /api/v1/ (the same answer, the same roles, plus the header X-API-Version) and three routes are added: /api/v1/me (who is asking, with the role, the accounts and what the session may do), /api/v1/repos (the repositories in pages) and /api/v1/openapi.json. Read only: nothing can be changed through it.
cfg.h.api.experimental_routes: Off by default. The routes the contract does not freeze (the streams, the files, the screens, the updates and a few more, each with its reason in docs/schemas/api_contract.json) answer 404 under /api/v1/ and are left out of /api/v1/openapi.json. On: they answer there too and the document lists them marked as experimental; they may change between versions. The old routes under /api/ never change.
cfg.h.cli.prefer_v1: On by default. monitor_cli.py asks the routes the contract freezes under /api/v1/ and, when the monitor answers 404 there (the read API is closed, see api.v1_enabled), asks the old route and does not try the prefix again. The answers are the same by both ways; off = always the old routes. The variable MONITOR_CLI_PREFER_V1 (0 or 1) wins over this setting.
cfg.h.api.default_limit: Default 50. How many items a list of the API returns when the client does not ask for a number with limit=. It cannot be above the maximum below.
cfg.h.api.max_limit: Default 200. The largest number a client may ask for with limit=; a larger number is refused with the error api.bad_limit.
cfg.h.api.cursor_ttl_seconds: Default 900. The cursor that comes with each page (next_cursor) is signed and stops working after this many seconds; the client then starts the list again.
cfg.h.api.gzip_min_bytes: Default 1024. An answer of the own routes of the API (me, repos) is compressed with gzip when the client accepts it and the answer has at least this many bytes. 0 never compresses.
api.bad_cursor: The page cursor is not valid, belongs to another query or has expired; start the list again.
api.bad_limit: limit must be a whole number from 1 to {max}.
api.unknown_field: The field {field} is not part of the answer; ask only for fields the contract lists.
api.bad_profile: profile must be full or compact.
api.server_error: The server could not answer this request; try again later.
cfg.f.upstream.enabled: Follow the original repository of each fork
cfg.h.upstream.enabled: Off by default. For every fork it reads the original repository (the upstream) it was copied from: the state of the checks of the last commit of its default branch and its latest release, and shows them in the hygiene panel of the Sentinel. It costs one request for several forks (see the limits below) and writes nothing anywhere.
cfg.f.upstream.refresh_hours: Hours between two readings of a fork
cfg.h.upstream.refresh_hours: Default 12. A fork is read again only after this many hours; the forks are taken in turn, the least recently read first.
cfg.h.upstream.requests_per_hour: Default 6. The most requests this follow may make in an hour. With 8 forks per request that is 48 forks an hour; a larger account is covered in several turns.
cfg.h.upstream.forks_per_request: Default 8 (1 to 25). How many forks are read in one request.
cfg.f.upstream.news_days: Days a new release counts as news
cfg.h.upstream.news_days: Default 7. A release that appears in the original is marked as new for this many days.
cfg.f.upstream.notify: Tell me when the original is red or has a new release
cfg.h.upstream.notify: Off by default. On: an information notice (never an error) for each followed fork whose original has red checks or published a new release in the last days. Off: the data is only shown in the panel.
cfg.h.upstream.repos: Names of the forks to follow. Empty (default): every fork of the account, within the limits above.
evt.upstream_red: The original of {repo} ({parent}) has red checks on its default branch
ui.upstream_summary: {n} forks followed: {red} with a red original, {news} with a new release, {unread} not read yet
ui.upstream_round: One pass over the {n} forks takes {hours} h at this pace, longer than the {refresh} h between readings: the follow-up never rests.
cfg.f.ci.disabled_apart: A workflow switched off by hand is not red
cfg.f.ci.dependabot_alerts: Alert when the Dependabot updates fail
cfg.h.ci.disabled_apart: On by default. A workflow that the owner switched off by hand (state disabled_manually) leaves the list of reds and is counted apart: switching it off is the answer to its failure, and its last run would stay failed for ever. A workflow that GitHub switched off for inactivity is not affected (that is not a decision of the owner). Off: a switched-off workflow stays red until it runs green.
cfg.h.ci.dependabot_alerts: On by default. A failed run of the workflow "Dependabot Updates" (the dependency updates that GitHub makes for itself) becomes an alert of its own with medium severity (level warning, code ci.dependabot_failed), one per repository. It is never a red of the repository, because there is no file to fix. You can silence it like any alert. Off: the failure only appears in the services of the sentinel panel.
cfg.h.ci.copilot_alerts: Off by default. The workflows of Copilot (code review and coding agent) are information, never red: their failures are listed among the services of the sentinel and never make a repository red. With this switch each failed one also becomes a notice (level info, code ci.copilot_activity) in the Alerts tab; it can be silenced like any alert.

cfg.h.ops.backup.enabled: Off by default. On, the monitor makes a complete package every interval, keeps the newest ones and records the result (a failure is written down and never stops the monitor). A copy made by hand works whatever this says.
cfg.h.ops.backup.dir: Where the copies are written. A relative path starts at the data folder (default: backups). A path with .. or on a network share is refused.
cfg.h.ops.backup.interval_hours: Hours between two scheduled copies (1 to 720). Default 24.
cfg.h.ops.backup.keep: How many copies stay in the folder; the oldest ones with the name of a copy are removed after each new one (1 to 365). Default 7.
cfg.h.ops.backup.include_config: On: the package also carries the settings of the page and the lists (targets, ecosystems, profiles), cleaned of every secret: only the settings the page can show travel, never a token, a key or the value of a variable. Off: only the data.
cfg.h.ops.backup.compress_level: Compression of the package, 0 (none) to 9 (smallest). Default 6.
cfg.h.ops.backup.encrypt: Off by default. On, every copy is sealed with AES-256-GCM using the key held by the variable named below. It needs the optional library cryptography: without it (or without a key of 12 characters or more) the copy is REFUSED with a clear message, never made in the clear and never sealed with something weaker.
cfg.h.ops.backup.key_env: The NAME of the environment variable that holds the key (for example GHAMON_BACKUP_KEY). Only the name is a setting; the key itself is never written in the configuration, shown or put in a copy.
cfg.h.ops.purge.enabled: Off by default. On, an administrator on this computer can run the retention purge now (the page and the API show first what would be removed). It never runs by itself.
cfg.h.ops.purge.require_backup_hours: A purge on demand is refused unless a good copy is newer than this many hours (0 to 720; 0 does not ask). Default 24.
cfg.h.ops.doctor.strict_exit: Off by default. On, a warning of the doctor makes it exit 3 (a failure is always 1), which suits a cron job that must notice warnings. --strict does the same for one run.
cfg.h.ops.doctor.backup_max_age_days: The doctor warns when the last good copy is older than this many days (1 to 365) or when there is none and the schedule is on. Default 8.
cfg.h.ops.doctor.min_free_mb: The doctor warns when the volume of the data has less free space than this (50 to 10000000 MB). Default 500.
cfg.h.ops.doctor.sqlite_check: How the doctor looks at a SQLite database: quick (quick_check, fast, the default), deep (integrity_check, slow on big files) or off. It opens the file read only and stops at the time limit.
cfg.h.ops.doctor.sqlite_timeout_s: Seconds the integrity check of SQLite may take before the doctor stops it and warns (1 to 600). Default 20.
cfg.h.ops.doctor.webhook_min_length: The doctor warns when the shared secret of the webhook is shorter than this many characters (8 to 128). Only the length is compared; the secret is never shown. Default 16.
doctor.f.volumes: A folder the monitor writes to is read only, missing or owned by another user (a Docker volume mounted as root, for example). Give the user of the monitor write permission, or mount the volume read-write.
doctor.f.supervisor: The monitor that is running reports a stuck or dead refresh cycle, or a supervisor that does not answer. Read the deep health check (monitor_cli.py health --deep) and restart the monitor if it persists.
doctor.f.limits: The webhook is on without a shared secret, or the secret is shorter than the minimum, or retention is off on a service. Put a long random value in the variable named by webhook.secret_env and keep retention on.
doctor.f.sqlite_hot: A database failed the integrity check (a power cut or a full disk can do it) or the check ran out of time. Restore the last good backup (monitor_cli.py backup restore) or raise ops.doctor.sqlite_timeout_s.
doctor.f.backup_age: There is no recent good backup. Make one now (monitor_cli.py backup create) or turn on the scheduled copy (ops.backup.enabled).
doctor.t.disk: Free disk space of the data
doctor.f.disk: The volume of the data is nearly full. Free space, move the data folder to a bigger volume or lower the days of retention.
doctor.f.metrics: The Prometheus output is on but /metrics does not answer well. Check the settings of the output and the access to the page of this computer.
ops.err.busy: Another backup is being made right now; try again when it is done.
ops.err.purge_off: The purge on demand is switched off (ops.purge.enabled).
ops.err.purge_no_backup: There is no good backup newer than ops.purge.require_backup_hours: make one first.

cfg.h.sentinels.supply.enabled: Reads, without writing anything, the workflow files of each repository (no clone needed) and flags what lets a moved tag or an outsider act with the repository's token. Off by default.
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.refresh_seconds: Seconds between two rounds of the Supply chain sentinel.
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.max_repos_per_tic: At most this many repositories are read in one round.
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.deadline_s: Seconds. A round stops starting new repositories when this time has passed; the ones not reached keep waiting (the oldest read goes first next round) and are listed by name as not checked instead of counting as zero alerts. 0 = no ceiling.
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.max_calls_per_tic: At most this many calls to GitHub are made in one round: one to list the workflows of a repository and one more for each file that is new or changed.
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.max_files_per_rep: A repository with more workflow files than this is read only in part and is listed as incomplete.
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.min_rate_remainin: The sentinel pauses while the GitHub allowance left is below this.
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.repos: All the repositories, or the ones of some ecosystems, or a list of names.
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.ignore: Patterns repository:file:rule (with * for any) of findings to leave out, for example myrepo:release.yml:unpinned_uses. A comment `# monitor-lint: ignore RULE` in the file does the same.
Actions not pinned to a commit
Raises an alert for each repository with a `uses:` that is not pinned to a full commit SHA: whoever owns the action can move the tag.
Actions not pinned to a commit: level
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
supply.t.unpinned: {repo}: {n} actions are not pinned to a full commit SHA ({files} files)
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.signals.mutable_r: Raises an alert for each repository with a `uses:` that follows a branch such as main or master, which changes with every push of the owner.
cfg.f.sentinels.supply.signals.mutable_r: Actions on a moving branch: level
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.signals.mutable_r: Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
supply.t.mutable_ref: {repo}: {n} actions follow a moving branch ({files} files)
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.signals.permissio: Raises an alert for each repository with a workflow that gives the token `permissions: write-all`.
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
supply.t.permissions_wide: {repo}: {n} workflows give the token write-all ({files} files)
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.signals.permissio: Raises an alert for each repository with a workflow that has no `permissions:` block, so the token gets the broader default.
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
supply.t.permissions_missing: {repo}: {n} workflows have no permissions block ({files} files)
cfg.h.sentinels.supply.signals.pr_target: Raises an alert for each repository with a workflow triggered by pull_request_target that checks out the code of the pull request.
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
supply.t.pr_target_checkout: {repo}: {n} workflows run pull request code with pull_request_target ({files} files)
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.enabled: Reads, without writing anything, the latest releases, tags, CHANGELOG and the version files you name of each repository (no clone needed) and flags what was built but not delivered. Off by default.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.refresh_seconds: Seconds between two rounds of the Delivery sentinel.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.max_repos_per_t: At most this many repositories are read in one round of the Delivery sentinel.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.deadline_s: Seconds. A round stops starting new repositories when this time has passed; the ones not reached keep waiting (the oldest read goes first next round) and are listed by name as not checked instead of counting as zero alerts. 0 = no ceiling.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.max_calls_per_t: At most this many calls to GitHub are made in one round: one or two per repository for releases and tags, one for the CHANGELOG and one for each version file.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.min_rate_remain: The Delivery sentinel pauses while the GitHub allowance left is below this.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.repos: All the repositories, or the ones of some ecosystems, or a list of names.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.unreleased_days: A repository whose CHANGELOG has entries under [Unreleased] raises its alert once the latest published release is older than this many days.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.unreleased_min_: The number of entries under [Unreleased] that a CHANGELOG needs before the unreleased signal can raise an alert.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.changelog_paths: Paths inside each repository where the CHANGELOG may be; the first one that exists is read.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.version_files: Paths inside each repository of files that declare its version (a JSON file with a version key, pyproject.toml, a line `version = ...`). Without any, the signal that compares versions only has the CHANGELOG and stays quiet.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.expected_assets: Patterns of file names (with * for any) that the latest release of a repository must carry, for example *.zip or SHA256SUMS*. Empty means no check.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.signals.unrelea: Raises an alert for each repository whose CHANGELOG has entries under [Unreleased] while its latest published release is old.
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
delivery.t.unreleased_pending: {repo}: {n} entries wait under Unreleased and the release {tag} is {days} days old
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.signals.tag_wit: Raises an alert for each repository with a version tag newer than its latest published release that has no release of its own.
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.signals.release: Raises an alert for each repository whose latest published release has an empty description.
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.signals.version: Raises an alert for each repository whose version files and CHANGELOG do not all declare the same version.
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.signals.ecosyst: Raises an alert for each repository that pins an older version than the latest release of the repository that provides a shared contract (the pin tables of the readiness settings).
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.
delivery.t.ecosystem_drift: {repo}: pins an older version than {current} of a shared contract
cfg.h.sentinels.delivery.signals.assets_: Raises an alert for each repository whose latest published release lacks a file for one of the expected patterns.
Level of the alert of this signal: info, warning, error or critical.

ui.upd_confirm:
Update from {from} to {to}.

What will happen:
1. The zip of the release is downloaded and its SHA-256 is compared with SHA256SUMS ({verified}).
2. A copy of the current version, its configuration and its data is made first in:
{backups}
3. The new files are put in place; your configuration, data, keys and logs are not replaced, and the configuration is migrated ({changes} change(s) to settings).
4. The monitor stops by itself, starts again with the new version and this page reconnects.
5. If the new version does not start, the previous one is put back and started.

Nothing else is touched. Do you want to continue?
ui.upd_back_confirm: Go back to {to}? The monitor stops by itself, the files of the last update are replaced by the copy made before it (your data too when its format changed) and the monitor starts again.
ui.upd_verified_no: NOT verified: the release has no SHA256SUMS
ui.upd_trust: The check compares the zip with SHA256SUMS, and both come from the same GitHub release: it detects a damaged or incomplete download, not a release that was replaced at its source. Trust in the release rests on GitHub and on your own account there.
ui.upd_restarting: The monitor is restarting; this page reconnects by itself.
ui.upd_failed: The update did not finish; the previous version was put back where it could.
ui.upd_stopped: The update process stopped without a result. Look at logs/updater_handover.log.
ui.upd_lite: The Lite edition only tells you that a newer version exists. Update the Complete edition or use the updater of the command line.
ui.upd_blocked_lite: Updating from this page is not available in the Lite edition.
ui.upd_blocked_container: This monitor runs in a container: the image is replaced, not this page. Use the Docker documents.
ui.upd_blocked_service: This monitor is run by a service manager, which would start it again before the update could be applied. Update it with the updater of the command line, as the service document says.
ui.upd_blocked_demo: The demo does not update anything.
ui.upd_blocked_tool_missing: tools/monitor_updater.py is not in this folder, so the update cannot be applied from here.
ui.upd_blocked_account: Each account of the team mode is updated from the supervisor, not from its own page.
ui.upd_need_local: Applying an update needs an administrator at the computer where the monitor runs.
ui.upd_err_blocked: The plan is blocked: see the checks.
ui.upd_err_no_previous: There is no earlier version to go back to.
ui.upd_err_cooldown: Too many failed attempts: wait a few minutes before trying again.
ui.upd_err_local_only: Only from the computer where the monitor runs.

cfg.h.ai.assistant.enabled: Off. On = the Alerts tab shows a panel of fixed questions that the AI answers from the data of the monitor. It only reads, never acts, shows its sources and needs an AI provider (ai.provider).

cfg.h.ai.assistant.tools: From the closed list: status, alerts, runs, score; one per line. Every one only reads what the monitor already holds; none writes or reaches GitHub.
cfg.h.ai.assistant.max_tool_calls: The most readings of the monitor's own data one question may make. 0 = it reads nothing and cannot answer.
cfg.h.ai.untrusted_text_max: Titles and names written in a repository are cut to this size before the AI sees them, and are handed over as data between marks, never as instructions.

cfg.h.ai.airgapped: Off. On = the AI only talks to a model on this computer or on a private address you declared below; any address of the internet and any cloud service is refused before a connection is opened. The general air-gapped switch turns it on too. It can only be changed from this computer.
cfg.h.ai.airgap_hosts: Only used in air-gapped mode: names or addresses of your own network (192.168.1.20, gpu.lan) where a model runs; one per line. This computer is always allowed; a public address is refused even if listed.
cfg.h.ai.redact.extra_terms: Words (a server, a project) that are replaced by [hidden] in every text before the AI sees it, whatever their case. They add to the secrets the monitor already hides; they never replace them.
ai.airgap_cloud_provider: Air-gapped mode is on: this provider is a service of the internet and is refused.
ai.airgap_host_not_allowed: Air-gapped mode is on: {host} is not on this computer and is not in the list of private addresses you declared.
ai.airgap_no_address: Air-gapped mode is on: the provider has no address that can be checked.
ai.doc_egress_ok: Air-gapped mode is on and this provider is on this computer or on an address you declared.
ai.doc_egress_blocked: Air-gapped mode is on and it refuses this provider: {why}
cfg.h.ai.similar.enabled: Off. On = "explain this alert" also lists the alerts that look like it (open ones and resolved ones the feed remembers), found by a plain comparison of words: no model, no embeddings, only the data of this account.
cfg.h.ai.similar.max: The most alerts that look alike that are listed next to an explanation.

cfg.h.sentinel.trend_green_pct: Share of green workflows (%) under which the line of the daily trend is crossed. 90 by default. Only changes the line drawn in the chart, never an alert. Applies after a restart.
cfg.h.sentinel.trend_health: Mean health (0 to 100) under which the line of the daily trend is crossed. 70 by default. Only changes the line drawn in the chart, never an alert. Applies after a restart.
cfg.f.sentinel.trend_quota_pct: Line of the API quota used
cfg.h.sentinel.trend_quota_pct: Share of the API quota used (%) above which the line of the daily trend is crossed. 80 by default. Only changes the line drawn in the chart, never an alert. Applies after a restart.
cfg.h.ai.redact.extra_patterns: Off (empty). One per line; a pattern describes a whole word and has only three wildcards: * (any run of characters), ? (one character) and # (one digit), for example deploy-* or *.corp-name. It is not a regular expression, so it cannot make the monitor hang. At least 3 plain characters, 80 at most.
cfg.h.ai.prompt_log.enabled: Off. On = every question sent to the AI and its answer are written, already cleaned of secrets and of your hidden words, to ai_prompts.jsonl in the folder of the logs, for an administrator to read or empty. It is not in the backup or in the zip. A cached answer is not written.
cfg.h.ai.prompt_log.keep: How many of the newest lines the record keeps; older ones are dropped.
ai.doc_model_retired: The model {model} is in your list of retired models (config/ai_models.json): it is skipped and the next of the chain answers.
ui.pl_help: The questions sent to the AI and its answers, already cleaned of secrets and of your hidden words, kept in a local file while ai.prompt_log.enabled is on. Only an administrator can read or empty it.
ui.pl_denied: Only an administrator on this computer can do this.
cfg.t.ai.assistant.enabled: You will see: a panel of fixed questions in the Alerts tab, answered by your AI from the data the monitor holds. Cost: one AI call per question, inside the daily budget of the AI; nothing is written and GitHub is not called.
cfg.t.ai.prompt_log.enabled: You will see: in Settings, a card that lists the last prompts sent to the AI and their answers, cleaned of secrets. Cost: a small local file; only an administrator can read or empty it.
cfg.t.ai.similar.enabled: You will see: "explain this alert" also lists alerts that look like it, found by comparing words. Cost: none from the AI and none from GitHub; it only reads what the monitor already holds.
cfg.t.ai.airgapped: You will see: the AI refuses every address that is not this computer or a private address you list, before any connection is opened. Cost: none; a cloud model stops working while it is on.
cfg.t.api.v1_enabled: You will see: the read API for clients under /api/v1/ (auto opens it when the monitor runs as a service). Cost: none; it only reads and follows the same roles as the page.
cfg.h.savings.webhook_live_per_repo: Judge the webhook repository by repository: a quiet repository is spared its slow read only if an event of its own arrived lately. A repository whose webhook was never set up or broke is then read as always. It spares fewer reads. Works together with Webhook first.
cfg.t.savings.webhook_live_per_repo: You will see: with Webhook first on, only the repositories that sent an event of their own lately skip their slow read; the Webhook panel also counts them. Cost: none; it reads fewer repositories less often, so it spares fewer calls.
